sections.title: Grammar
sections.html:
Read across. A reads from the left side. B answers from the right side. Choose one part from each column.

Grammar Box 1: Offers with I'll

PROBLEM
The phone's ringing.
These boxes are heavy.
We need chairs for the party.
I don't have a ride.
I forgot my pen.
→
OFFER (I'll = I will)
I'llget it. / answer it.
I'llcarry them. / help you.
I'llbring them. / set them up.
I'llgive you a ride. / pick you up.
I'lllend you one. / lend you mine.

Grammar Box 2: Promises: Will you…?

QUESTION
Willyoucall me tonight? / be there at five?
Willyouremember? / be late?
→
ANSWER
Yes, I will.I promise.
No, I won't.Sorry, I'm busy.
Don't worry.I won't forget. / I won't be late.

Grammar Box 3: Other ways to offer (understand and answer)

OFFER
Do you want me tocarry that? / open the door?
Shall Icall a taxi? / close the window?
→
ANSWER
Yes, please. Thanks! / No, thanks. I'm OK.
Yes, please. That's very kind. / No, thanks.

Grammar Box 4: will (decided now) or going to (planned before)?

will: I decide NOW
A: We need drinks. B: OK, I'll bring juice.
A: The phone's ringing. B: I'll get it.
A: It's cold in here. B: I'll close the window.
→
going to: I PLANNED IT BEFORE
I'm going to bake a cake. (I bought eggs yesterday.)
We're going to visit my mother. (We bought tickets.)
She's going to work on Saturday. (It's on her schedule.)

Questions and answers

Q: Does will change for he or she?

A: No. I will, he will, she will, they will. Then use the base verb: She'll call (not wills, not will to call). I'll = I will; won't = will not.

Q: When do I use will?

A: For something you decide now: an offer (I'll help you), a promise (I'll call you back), or a quick decision (I'll have the soup).

Q: When do I use going to?

A: For a plan you made before: I'm going to visit my sister on Sunday. (I bought the ticket last week.)

Q: How do I say it?

A: I'll is one short sound (like aisle). won't sounds like don't. want is different: I want pizza.

Practice A: Write 'll, won't, or Will.

  1. A: It's cold in here. B: I____ close the window.
  2. Don't worry, I ____________ forget.
  3. A: I don't have a pen. B: I____ lend you one.
  4. I promise I ____________ be late.
  5. A: Can someone help me? B: I____ help you!
  6. ____________ you call me tonight?

Practice B: Circle the right words.

  1. A: The phone's ringing! B: OK, (I'll get / I'm going to get) it.
  2. I bought eggs and flour yesterday. I (will bake / am going to bake) a cake on Saturday.
  3. A: We need someone to clean up. B: (I'll do / I'm going to do) it!
  4. We have tickets. We (will see / are going to see) a movie tonight.
  5. A: Oh no, I forgot my lunch. B: (I'll share / I'm going to share) mine.
  6. She (will / is going to) visit her mother next week. She bought the bus ticket.

Common mistakes

✗ Don't say✓ Say
The phone's ringing. I answer it.The phone's ringing. I'll answer it.
I will to bring the drinks.I will bring (I'll bring) the drinks.
She wills call you.She will call you.
Don't worry, I don't forget.Don't worry, I won't forget.
Will you calling me?Will you call me?
I'll visit my sister Sunday. (I bought the ticket.)I'm going to visit my sister on Sunday.

Nota para hispanohablantes: en español muchas veces usamos el presente para ofrecer ayuda: ¿Te ayudo? Yo lo traigo. En inglés se necesita will: I'll help you. I'll bring it. (no I help you, no I bring it). won't = will not: I won't forget = No me voy a olvidar.

Tip for speakers of other languages: will never changes: I will, she will, they will. No -s and no to after it.

lessons.teacher:
How to Use This Plan

You don't need to speak Spanish or any other language. Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. Each Grammar page has one short Spanish note and one tip for speakers of other languages. Learners read them on their own. You never need to read, translate, or explain them.

Instructions: use the same short task words every week: Listen. Circle. Check. Write. Work with a partner. Work in a group. Ask a follow-up question. Learners have the Task Words page from Lesson 1.

Instruction rule: Model it (do it with one learner while everyone watches), check it (ask: "Do you write or speak? How many people do you talk to?"), then go. Say less, show more.

Grouping toolkit: Pairs: turn to a neighbor; with an odd number, make one group of 3. Groups: 3–4 learners. Inside–outside circles: the inner circle faces out, the outer circle faces in; the outer circle moves one person to the right each round. Mingle: everyone stands and talks to many classmates. The teacher joins a pair only if one learner is left over.

When a learner is stuck or speaks another language to you: (1) show it: the picture, a gesture, or the board; (2) give one more short English example; (3) point to the grammar box on their page; (4) a classmate can help for a few seconds, then back to English. You don't need to understand what classmates say to each other.

Lesson 5 (Week 5): Don't Worry, I'll Do It

At a glance

Objectives: learners can…

  • offer help with I'll… (The phone's ringing. I'll get it.)
  • make a promise (I'll call you back. Don't worry, I won't forget.)
  • ask and answer Will you…? → Yes, I will. / No, I won't.
  • understand Do you want me to…? and Shall I…?
  • choose will (decided now) or going to (planned before)
  • read a school flyer and a sign-up sheet, and write a short text message offering help

Materials

  • Student Pages for Lesson 5 (print for the number expected + 3 spares)
  • Talk Time: the Problem Cards and the Event Board (on the Talk Time pages)
  • phone + small speaker, L3_L5_listening.mp3
  • optional: a heavy bag or a box to show carry and offer
  • Prep time: 10 min.

Key vocabulary (with pictures on the New Words page)

★ offer • ★ promise • ★ carry • ★ set up • ★ clean up • ★ bring • ★ lend • ★ give a ride • ★ call back • ★ text • school event • flyer

Clock-time plan

Times are loose. If a step runs long, take time from Read & Write first, then from Talk Time.

TimeStepMinGrouping (15 / 7–8)If running behind
6:00–6:10Opening Talk + Homework Check10Pairs (7 pairs + 1 trio / 3–4 pairs)One card only
6:10–6:18New Words (picture page) + pair game8Whole class, then pairsTeach the ★ words only
6:18–6:30Listening: play 1 (Task A), play 2 (Tasks B and C) + "Say it"12Individuals, then pairs checkDo Task C together on the board
6:30–6:45Grammar Q&A: I'll…; Will you…?; will vs. going to + pair drill15Whole class, then pairsSkip the pair drill; Talk Time practices it
6:45–7:00BREAK15
7:00–7:12Talk Time: Problem / Offer Cards + Event Board12Pairs, then groups of 3–4Round 1 only
7:12–7:17Exit Ticket + Homework5IndividualsNever skip
7:17–7:25Read & Write: a flyer + a sign-up sheet; a text message8Individuals, then pairsReading questions only; the text becomes homework
7:25–7:30Progress Check5IndividualsDo it in Week 6 at 6:00, while people arrive

Skip order if you're running behind: (1) the Read & Write text message (it becomes homework); (2) the pair drill at the end of Grammar; (3) half of Talk Time (Round 1 only). Never skip: the listening tasks, the grammar boxes and the mistakes table, and the exit ticket.

Attendance (15 → 7–8): every step lists both sizes. With 5 or fewer, sit at one table: Round 1 goes around the table (each person reads a card to the next person), and Round 2 is one group.

Step by step

Step 1 · 6:00–6:10 · Opening Talk + Homework Check · 10 min

  • Grouping: pairs, the same partner for both parts. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs.
  • Before class: write on the board: What were you doing at…? I was…ing when…
  • Opening Talk (6 min): learners open the Opening Talk page. A asks a card question; B answers with 2–3 sentences; A asks one follow-up. Switch after each card.
  • Model with one learner: "What were you doing at 8:00 last night?" → (answer) → "Really? Who were you with?"
  • Homework Check (4 min): partners read their Lesson 4 Homework item 1 (At 7:00 a.m., I was…) to each other. Walk around. Write 2 common errors on the board (often I was cook or They was…) and correct them together.
  • Late arrivals: join any pair as a group of 3.
  • If behind: one card only, then the homework check.

Step 2 · 6:10–6:18 · New Words · 8 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Show the New Words page.
  • Do: point to each picture and say the word. Learners repeat once. Act out carry (pick up a bag), offer (raise your hand: "I'll help!"), promise (hand on your heart: "I promise"), and clean up (sweep).
  • Show offer: pick up a heavy bag and look tired. Wait. When a learner says something, smile: "Thank you! That's an offer." Then say it for them: "I'll carry it."
  • Check meaning (1 min): "You give your pen to a classmate for 5 minutes. Is that lend or give?" (lend) • "You drive your neighbor to work. You…?" (give a ride) • "Before a party, you put out the chairs. You…?" (set up) • "After the party?" (clean up)
  • Pairs (2 min): A says a word; B points to the picture and makes a sentence (I can give you a ride.). Switch.
  • If behind: teach the ★ words only.

Step 3 · 6:18–6:30 · Listening + "Say it" · 12 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Before you listen (1 min): point to the school event picture on the New Words page. Say: "Carmen and David are parents. Their children go to Hillside School. Carmen is calling David. What is the event? Listen."
  • Play 1 → Task A (what is the event?). Pairs compare. Check together.
  • Read Tasks B and C together (1 min) so learners know what to listen for. For Task B, show the letters: D = David, R = Rosa, S = David's sister, C = Carmen.
  • Play 2 → Tasks B and C. Pairs compare. Then show the answers (answer key).
  • "Say it" (2 min): say: "I will is usually I'll: one short sound." Read I'll, you'll, we'll. Then contrast won't (like don't) and want: I won't forget. / I want pizza. The class repeats each line twice.
  • The audio plays the conversation once (about 1:17). Press play again for play 2. A third play is fine if the class needs it.
  • If behind: do Task C together on the board, reading the lines yourself.

Step 4 · 6:30–6:45 · Grammar Q&A · 15 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Show the Grammar page. The left side is the problem or the question. The right side is the answer.
  • Box 1 (3 min): act it out. Drop a pen: "Oh no!" A learner picks it up: "I'll get it." Read Box 1: you read the problem; the class answers with I'll….
  • Box 2 (3 min): promises. Ask a learner: "Will you bring your homework next week?" → "Yes, I will." → "Promise?" → "I promise. I won't forget." Point to won't = will not.
  • Box 3 (1 min): Do you want me to…? / Shall I…? are other ways to offer. Learners only need to understand them and answer Yes, please. / No, thanks.
  • Box 4 (3 min): draw two pictures on the board: a light bulb (an idea now → I'll) and a calendar (planned before → I'm going to). Read Box 4 across.
  • Check questions: "The phone's ringing. I ___ get it." ('ll) • "I bought a ticket. I ___ visit my mom." ('m going to) • "Don't worry, I ___ forget." (won't)
  • Practice A and B (3 min): learners write, then pairs check. Go over the answers.
  • Pair drill (last 2 min): A says a problem (I'm hungry. / It's cold. / My bag is heavy.); B offers help with I'll…. Switch.
  • If behind: skip the pair drill. Talk Time practices it.

Break · 6:45–7:00 · 15 min

  • Write on the board: I'll… / Don't worry, I won't… / Thanks! That's very kind. and I'm going to… (I planned it.)

Step 5 · 7:00–7:12 · Talk Time: Problem / Offer Cards + Event Board · 12 min

  • Grouping: Round 1 pairs; Round 2 groups of 3–4. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 trio, then 4 groups. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs, then 2 groups. 5 or fewer: one group for both rounds.
  • Round 1, pairs (5 min): A reads a problem card (My car won't start.). B offers help with I'll… and one reason or detail (I'll give you a ride, because I'm going that way.). A says thank you (Thanks! That's very kind.). Switch after each card. Try to use all 8 cards.
  • Model with one learner (1 min): read card 1. Help the learner say "I'll give you a ride." Answer: "Really? Thank you so much!"
  • Round 2, groups (6 min): each group chooses one event on the Event Board: a park cleanup or a school family night. Each person volunteers for two jobs with I'll… and writes their name. Then each person says one plan with going to (something they planned before): I'm going to work on Saturday morning, so I'll come at 11:00.
  • Share (1 min): one person from each group reads their board: "Ana will bring water. Tom will set up the tables."
  • If behind: Round 1 only.

Step 6 · 7:12–7:17 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP

  • Exit ticket: each learner writes two sentences on a slip: one offer or promise with I'll or I won't, and one plan with going to and because or so (I'm going to visit my sister on Sunday, because it's her birthday.). Collect at the door.
  • Homework: open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (one offer on the board). Say: "About 15 minutes. Bring it next week."

Read & Write · 7:17–7:25 · A Flyer, a Sign-Up Sheet, and a Text Message · 8 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Read (3 min): learners read the flyer and the volunteer sign-up sheet and answer questions 1–5. Say: "Read fast first. Then find the answers."
  • Pairs check (1 min): compare answers; check together.
  • Write (4 min): learners choose one open job on the sign-up sheet and write a short text message to Carmen offering help, with I'll (and going to if they want). Show the example.
  • If behind: questions 1–5 only; the text message becomes homework.

Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min

  • Grouping: individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
  • Part A: read the 4 sentences in the answer key, slowly, 2 times each. Learners circle a (decided now) or b (planned before).
  • Parts B and C: learners do them alone. Walk around and help with the instructions only.
  • Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "With a little help." 😐 "Not yet."
  • Collect the pages (or check them at the start of Week 6).
  • If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 6 at 6:00, while learners arrive.

Listening script: L3_L5_listening.mp3 (about 1:17; the conversation plays once, so press play again for the second listen)

Audio: play from a phone + small speaker. No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer, at a normal, friendly speed.

Narrator: Lesson five. Listening. Carmen and David are parents at Hillside School. Carmen is calling David. Listen.

Carmen: Hi, David. It's Carmen. It's about the family night at school on Friday.

David: Oh, right. How can I help?

Carmen: We need someone to set up the tables and chairs.

David: No problem. I'll set them up. I'll come early, at five.

Carmen: Thank you! And Rosa is going to bring pizza. She ordered it yesterday.

David: Great. What about drinks?

Carmen: Hmm. No one has the drinks yet.

David: OK, I'll bring the drinks. Juice and water.

Carmen: Perfect. Can you also make a flyer?

David: I'm going to be very busy at work this week. But my sister can make one. I'll ask her and call you back tonight.

Carmen: Will you call me before eight?

David: Yes, I will. I promise. Don't worry, I won't forget.

Carmen: Thanks, David. I'm going to clean up after the event.

David: I'll help you clean up, too. See you on Friday!

Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Answer key

  • Listening Task A: b (a family night at a school).
  • Listening Task B: 1 D (set up the tables and chairs) • 2 R (bring pizza) • 3 D (bring drinks) • 4 S (make a flyer) • 5 D (call back tonight) • 6 C and D (clean up after the event: Carmen, and David helps).
  • Listening Task C: 1 'll, 2 going to, 3 'll, 4 going to, 5 'll, 6 going to.
  • Grammar Practice A: 1 'll, 2 won't, 3 'll, 4 won't, 5 'll, 6 Will.
  • Grammar Practice B: 1 I'll get, 2 am going to bake, 3 I'll do, 4 are going to see, 5 I'll share, 6 is going to.
  • Talk Time: answers will vary. Sample offers for the problem cards: 1 I'll give you a ride. 2 I'll lend you mine. 3 I'll help you carry them. 4 I'll call him for you. / I'll text him. 5 I'll help you clean up. 6 I'll set up the chairs. 7 I'll lend you an umbrella. 8 I'll show you. / I'll help you.
  • Homework 1: answers will vary; for example 1 I'll open the window. 2 I'll lend you a pen. 3 I'll make you a sandwich. 4 I'll help you carry it. Homework 2: 1 'll, 2 'm going to, 3 'll, 4 're going to, 5 won't, 6 Will. Homework 3 and 4: answers will vary.
  • Read & Write B: 1 on Friday, October 16, from 6:00 to 8:00 p.m. • 2 in the school gym, 240 Hill Road • 3 Rosa • 4 games for children and rides for families • 5 Carmen, at 555-0186 • Writing (C): answers will vary; for example Hi Carmen, this is Maya. I'll help with the games for the children. I'm going to finish work at 5:00, so I'll be there at 5:45.
  • Progress Check Part A (the teacher says, 2 times each): 1 "OK, I'll carry that box for you." → a • 2 "I'm going to visit my sister on Sunday. I bought the bus ticket." → b • 3 "Don't worry. I'll call you back in five minutes." → a • 4 "We're going to have a party next week. We sent the invitations." → b
  • Progress Check Part B: 1 will, 2 won't, 3 open, 4 are going to.
  • Progress Check Part C: answers will vary; for example 1 I'll carry it for you. 2 I'll give you a ride.
  • Progress Check scoring: A /4 + B /4 + C /2 = /10. This is not a test grade. It shows who needs more help hearing will vs. going to (A) and with the forms (B, C).

Teacher notes

  • Invented events (important): every event, job, and sign-up sheet in this lesson is invented. Volunteering is an example, not a request: never ask learners to sign up for a real event, give a real phone number, or offer a real ride. "I can't help this time" is always an OK answer.
  • will never changes: I will, she will, they will. No -s, no to: She'll call (not She wills call, not She will to call).
  • will or going to: I'll = I decide now (an offer, a promise, a quick decision). going to = I planned it before (I bought the ticket; I ordered the pizza). Don't spend a long time on cases where both are possible; in real life, both are often fine.
  • Shall I…? / Do you want me to…? are for understanding only this week. Learners answer Yes, please. / No, thanks, I'm OK.
  • Mixed levels: stronger learners add a reason to each offer (I'll drive, because I have a big car.). Newer learners use Box 1 as a script in Talk Time.
  • Typical mistakes this week: I help you (for an offer), I will to bring, She wills, Don't worry, I don't forget, I'll go to the dentist tomorrow (when it's already planned). Say the right form clearly; the learner repeats. Learners can read the Spanish note and the tip on their Grammar page themselves; you don't need to explain them.

sections.title: Grammar
sections.html:
Read across. A reads from the left side. B answers from the right side. Choose one part from each column.

Grammar Box 1: What will you do if…?

QUESTION
What will you doif the power goes out?
What will you doif it snows tomorrow?
What will you doif it's very hot?
→
ANSWER (If + present, will)
If the power goes out,I'll use a flashlight. / I'll call my landlord.
If it snows,I'll stay home. / I'll take the bus.
If it's very hot,I'll drink a lot of water. / I'll go to the library.

Grammar Box 2: The if part can go first or second

IF FIRST (comma)
If it rains, I'll take the bus.
If school closes, my kids will stay home.
→
IF SECOND (no comma)
I'll take the bus if it rains.
My kids will stay home if school closes.

Grammar Box 3: Will…? Short answers

QUESTION
If it snows tomorrow,will school be closed?
If the storm is bad,will the buses run?
→
ANSWER
Yes, it will. / Probably. / Maybe. / Probably not. / No, it won't.
Probably not. / Maybe. / I don't know.

Grammar Box 4: Predictions with probably and maybe

How sure?Prediction
100% sureIt will rain.
75% sureIt will probably rain.
50% sureMaybe it will rain.
25% sureIt probably won't rain.
0%It won't rain.

Grammar Box 5: Review: safety tips with should

QUESTION
What should we dobefore a storm?
→
ANSWER
You shouldbuy batteries. / keep bottled water at home. / charge your phone.
You shouldn'tuse candles. / drive in a flood.

Questions and answers

Q: Which verb comes after if?

A: The present: If it rains… (not If it will rain). Put will in the other half: …I'll stay home.

Q: Can I say If rains?

A: No. English needs a subject: If it rains. If it's hot.

Q: Where does probably go?

A: After will: It will probably rain. Before won't: It probably won't snow. Maybe goes first: Maybe it will snow.

Q: How do I say it?

A: it'll sounds like id-ul. Stress the important words: If the power goes out, we'll use a flashlight.

Practice A: Write the verbs.

  1. If it ____________ (rain), I ____________ (take) the bus.
  2. If the power ____________ (go) out, we ____________ (use) flashlights.
  3. She ____________ (stay) home if it ____________ (snow).
  4. If you ____________ (not / have) water, I ____________ (bring) some.
  5. If it ____________ (be) very hot, we ____________ (go) to the library.
  6. What ____________ you do if school ____________ (close)?

Practice B: Circle the right words.

  1. If it (rains / will rain), I'll stay home.
  2. It will (probably rain / rain probably) tonight.
  3. It (probably won't / won't probably) snow.
  4. If (it snows / snows), school will be closed.
  5. If the power goes out tonight, I (use / will use) a flashlight.
  6. You (should / should to) keep water at home.

Common mistakes

✗ Don't say✓ Say
If it will rain, I'll stay home.If it rains, I'll stay home.
If rains, I'll take the bus.If it rains, I'll take the bus.
If the power goes out, I use a flashlight. (tonight)If the power goes out, I'll use a flashlight.
It will rain probably.It will probably rain.
It won't probably snow.It probably won't snow.
You should to buy batteries.You should buy batteries.

Nota para hispanohablantes: es como si + presente en español: If it rains, I'll stay = Si llueve, me quedo / me quedaré. No uses will después de if: If it rains (no If it will rain). En inglés se necesita it: If it rains (no If rains).

Tip for speakers of other languages: never put will right after if. Put will in the other half of the sentence.

lessons.teacher:
How to Use This Plan

You don't need to speak Spanish or any other language. Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. Each Grammar page has one short Spanish note and one tip for speakers of other languages. Learners read them on their own. You never need to read, translate, or explain them.

Instructions: use the same short task words every week: Listen. Circle. Check. Write. Work with a partner. Work in a group. Ask a follow-up question. Learners have the Task Words page from Lesson 1.

Instruction rule: Model it (do it with one learner while everyone watches), check it (ask: "Do you write or speak? How many people do you talk to?"), then go. Say less, show more.

Grouping toolkit: Pairs: turn to a neighbor; with an odd number, make one group of 3. Groups: 3–4 learners. Inside–outside circles: the inner circle faces out, the outer circle faces in; the outer circle moves one person to the right each round. Mingle: everyone stands and talks to many classmates. The teacher joins a pair only if one learner is left over.

When a learner is stuck or speaks another language to you: (1) show it: the picture, a gesture, or the board; (2) give one more short English example; (3) point to the grammar box on their page; (4) a classmate can help for a few seconds, then back to English. You don't need to understand what classmates say to each other.

Lesson 6 (Week 6): Be Ready

At a glance

Objectives: learners can…

  • understand a short weather forecast and a weather alert
  • say what will happen if… (If the power goes out, I'll use a flashlight.)
  • ask and answer What will you do if…?
  • make predictions with probably and maybe (It will probably rain. It probably won't snow.)
  • give simple safety tips with should (review)
  • read a weather alert text and fill in a simple "My Ready Plan" card

Materials

  • Student Pages for Lesson 6 (print for the number expected + 3 spares)
  • Talk Time: the Scenario Cards and the group plan (on the Talk Time pages)
  • phone + small speaker, L3_L6_listening.mp3
  • optional: a real flashlight and a battery to show
  • Prep time: 10 min. Choose the weather that fits your area (see the teacher notes).

Key vocabulary (with pictures on the New Words page)

★ forecast • ★ storm • ★ snowstorm • ★ flood • ★ heat wave • ★ weather alert • ★ power outage • ★ flashlight • ★ battery • ★ emergency kit • ★ bottled water • shelter

Clock-time plan

Times are loose. If a step runs long, take time from Read & Write first, then from Talk Time.

TimeStepMinGrouping (15 / 7–8)If running behind
6:00–6:10Opening Talk + Homework Check10Pairs (7 pairs + 1 trio / 3–4 pairs)One card only
6:10–6:18New Words (picture page) + pair game8Whole class, then pairsTeach the ★ words only
6:18–6:30Listening: play 1 (Task A), play 2 (Tasks B and C) + "Say it"12Individuals, then pairs checkDo Task C together on the board
6:30–6:45Grammar Q&A: If…, …will…; probably / maybe; should review + pair drill15Whole class, then pairsSkip the pair drill; Talk Time practices it
6:45–7:00BREAK15
7:00–7:12Talk Time: What If? Chain + Ready Plan12Groups of 3–4Round 1 only
7:12–7:17Exit Ticket + Homework5IndividualsNever skip
7:17–7:25Read & Write: a weather alert text + a kit checklist; "My Ready Plan"8Individuals, then pairsReading questions only; the plan becomes homework
7:25–7:30Progress Check5IndividualsDo it in Week 7 at 6:00, while people arrive

Skip order if you're running behind: (1) the Read & Write plan card (it becomes homework); (2) the pair drill at the end of Grammar; (3) half of Talk Time (Round 1 only). Never skip: the listening tasks, the grammar boxes and the mistakes table, and the exit ticket.

Attendance (15 → 7–8): every step lists both sizes. With 5 or fewer, sit at one table: the chain goes around the table, and the whole table makes one Ready Plan.

Step by step

Step 1 · 6:00–6:10 · Opening Talk + Homework Check · 10 min

  • Grouping: pairs, the same partner for both parts. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs.
  • Before class: write on the board: I'll… / I'm going to… / Don't worry, I won't…
  • Opening Talk (6 min): learners open the Opening Talk page. A asks a card question or reads a problem; B answers with 2–3 sentences; A asks one follow-up. Switch after each card.
  • Model with one learner: "What are you going to do this weekend?" → (answer) → "Really? Who with?"
  • Homework Check (4 min): partners read their Lesson 5 Homework item 1 (offers with I'll) to each other. Walk around. Write 2 common errors on the board (often I help you or I will to…) and correct them together.
  • Late arrivals: join any pair as a group of 3.
  • If behind: one card only, then the homework check.

Step 2 · 6:10–6:18 · New Words · 8 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Show the New Words page.
  • Do: point to each picture and say the word. Learners repeat once. Act out heat wave (fan your face), snowstorm (shiver), and power outage (click a light switch: "Oh no! No lights!").
  • Group the words (1 min): draw three columns on the board: WEATHER (forecast, storm, snowstorm, flood, heat wave), PROBLEMS (weather alert, power outage), and BE READY (flashlight, battery, emergency kit, bottled water, shelter). Learners say where each word goes.
  • Check meaning (1 min): "No lights, no fridge, no TV. It's a…?" (power outage) • "Where do you put a flashlight, water, and batteries?" (an emergency kit) • "A safe public building for a storm?" (a shelter)
  • Pairs (2 min): A says a word; B points to the picture and makes a sentence (I have a flashlight in my kitchen.). Switch.
  • If behind: teach the ★ words only.

Step 3 · 6:18–6:30 · Listening + "Say it" · 12 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Before you listen (1 min): say: "First, you'll hear a weather alert on the radio. Then two roommates, Nadia and Ben, talk about it. What is the weather problem? Listen."
  • Play 1 → Task A (what is the weather problem?). Pairs compare. Check together.
  • Read Tasks B and C together (1 min) so learners know what to listen for.
  • Play 2 → Tasks B and C. Pairs compare. Then show the answers (answer key).
  • "Say it" (2 min): say: "It will is usually it'll. It sounds like id-ul." Read it'll, we'll, I'll and the line in the "Say it" box, stressing the key words: If the power goes out, we'll use a flashlight. The class repeats each line twice.
  • The audio plays once (about 1:16). Press play again for play 2. A third play is fine if the class needs it.
  • If behind: do Task C together on the board, reading the lines yourself.

Step 4 · 6:30–6:45 · Grammar Q&A · 15 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Show the Grammar page. The left side is the question or the if part. The right side is the answer.
  • Draw on the board: IF + present → will. Under it write: If it rains, I'll take the bus. Circle rains and say "present, no will." Circle 'll and say "the result: will."
  • Box 1 (3 min): read a question from the left; the class answers from the right. Then ask learners: "What will you do if it snows tomorrow?"
  • Box 2 (2 min): the two halves can change places: I'll stay home if it snows. No comma when if is in the middle.
  • Boxes 3 and 4 (3 min): draw a line from 0% to 100% on the board. Put won't at 0%, probably won't at 25%, maybe at 50%, probably at 75%, will at 100%. Read Boxes 3 and 4 across. Box 5 is a quick should review.
  • Check questions: "If it ___ tomorrow, I'll stay home." (snows) • "If the power goes out, we ___ use flashlights." ('ll) • "It will ___ rain." (probably) • "It ___ won't snow." (probably)
  • Practice A and B (3 min): learners write, then pairs check. Go over the answers.
  • Pair drill (last 2 min): A says "What will you do if…" + a problem (the bus doesn't come? / it's very hot tomorrow?); B answers with If…, I'll…. Switch.
  • If behind: skip the pair drill. Talk Time practices it.

Break · 6:45–7:00 · 15 min

  • Write on the board: If it snows, I'll… → If I…, I'll… and probably / maybe / probably not.

Step 5 · 7:00–7:12 · Talk Time: What If? Chain + Ready Plan · 12 min

  • Grouping: groups of 3–4. 15 learners: 4 groups. 7–8 learners: 2 groups. 5 or fewer: one group.
  • Round 1, the chain (5 min): the first person says a sentence from a start card (If it snows tomorrow, I'll stay home.). The next person starts with the end of that sentence (If I stay home, I'll cook soup.), and so on around the group. Keep going until the chain stops, then start a new card.
  • Model with two learners (1 min): "If it snows tomorrow, I'll stay home." → Learner 1: "If I stay home, I'll watch TV." → Learner 2: "If I watch TV, I'll…" Laugh at funny chains; that's fine.
  • Round 2, Ready Plan (6 min): each group gets one Scenario Card (a storm, a heat wave, or a power outage). Together they write 4 sentences with If…, we'll… and a list of 5 things for the emergency kit. Then one person presents the plan in 1 minute.
  • If behind: Round 1 only.

Step 6 · 7:12–7:17 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP

  • Exit ticket: each learner writes two sentences on a slip: one with If…, I'll…, and one prediction with probably and because or so (It will probably rain tomorrow, so I'll take my umbrella.). Collect at the door.
  • Homework: open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (one sentence on the board). Say: "About 15 minutes. Bring it next week."

Read & Write · 7:17–7:25 · A Weather Alert and a Ready Plan · 8 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Read (3 min): learners read the weather alert text and the kit checklist, and answer questions 1–5. Say: "Read fast first. Then find the answers."
  • Pairs check (1 min): compare answers; check together.
  • Write (4 min): learners fill in the "My Ready Plan" card. Say: "First names only. Don't write phone numbers or addresses." An invented plan is fine.
  • If behind: questions 1–5 only; the plan card becomes homework.

Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min

  • Grouping: individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
  • Part A: read the 4 sentences in the answer key, slowly, 2 times each. Learners circle a or b.
  • Parts B and C: learners do them alone. Walk around and help with the instructions only.
  • Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "With a little help." 😐 "Not yet."
  • Collect the pages (or check them at the start of Week 7).
  • If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 7 at 6:00, while learners arrive.

Listening script: L3_L6_listening.mp3 (about 1:16; it plays once, so press play again for the second listen)

Audio: play from a phone + small speaker. No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer, at a normal, friendly speed. The weather alert is read by the narrator.

Narrator: Lesson six. Listening. First, listen to a weather alert on the radio. Then listen to two roommates, Nadia and Ben.

Narrator: This is a weather alert for Green County. A big storm will arrive tonight at about nine o'clock. There will probably be strong wind and heavy rain. The power will probably go out in some areas.

Nadia: Ben, did you hear that? A storm is coming tonight.

Ben: Yes. If the power goes out, we won't have any lights.

Nadia: Do we have a flashlight?

Ben: We have one, but it doesn't have batteries. I'll buy some after work.

Nadia: Good. And if the power goes out, the fridge won't work.

Ben: Then we'll eat the food in the fridge first! I'll buy bottled water, too.

Nadia: Great. Should we buy candles?

Ben: No, candles aren't safe. We'll use the flashlight. And I'll charge our phones before nine.

Nadia: OK. If the storm is really bad, will we go to work tomorrow?

Ben: Probably not. It'll probably rain all night. I'll check the forecast in the morning.

Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Answer key

  • Listening Task A: b (a storm: strong wind and heavy rain).
  • Listening Task B (check ✓): ✓ 1 batteries, ✓ 2 bottled water, ✗ 3 candles, ✓ 4 charged phones, ✗ 5 a snow shovel, ✗ 6 a new fridge. (3 checks.)
  • Listening Task C: 1 goes, won't • 2 'll • 3 won't • 4 'll • 5 is • 6 'll.
  • Grammar Practice A: 1 rains, 'll take • 2 goes, 'll use • 3 'll stay, snows • 4 don't have, 'll bring • 5 is, 'll go • 6 will, closes.
  • Grammar Practice B: 1 rains, 2 probably rain, 3 probably won't, 4 it snows, 5 will use, 6 should.
  • Talk Time: answers will vary. Sample Ready Plan (power outage): If the power goes out, we'll use flashlights. If the fridge doesn't work, we'll eat the cold food first. If our phones die, we'll use a radio with batteries. If it's very cold, we'll wear coats. Kit: flashlight, batteries, bottled water, food in cans, a first aid kit.
  • Homework 1–4: answers will vary. Homework 2 example: It will probably be sunny tomorrow. It probably won't snow.
  • Read & Write B: 1 a heat wave • 2 from Tuesday to Friday • 3 about 100 degrees • 4 from 12:00 to 5:00 p.m. • 5 at Oak Park Library, from 9:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. • Writing (C): answers will vary.
  • Progress Check Part A (the teacher says, 2 times each): 1 "If it snows tomorrow, I'll stay home." → a • 2 "It will probably rain tonight." → a • 3 "If the power goes out, we'll use flashlights." → b • 4 "It probably won't be hot tomorrow." → b
  • Progress Check Part B: 1 rains, 2 'll call, 3 probably won't, 4 it snows.
  • Progress Check Part C: answers will vary; for example 1 If the power goes out, I'll use a flashlight. 2 It will probably rain this weekend.
  • Progress Check scoring: A /4 + B /4 + C /2 = /10. This is not a test grade. It shows who needs more help hearing if sentences and predictions (A) and with the forms (B, C).

Teacher notes

  • Choose your weather: use the weather that fits your area (snow, heat, storms, floods). Skip a word that never happens where you live, or teach it quickly for the news.
  • Safety (important): keep candles out of practice plans (fire risk); use flashlights. Never use a grill or a generator inside. Use local alert systems only as examples. Don't do real sign-ups in class. Say once: "In a real emergency, call 911."
  • Feelings: some learners have lived through a hurricane, a flood, or an earthquake. Keep the stories in the lesson invented. Never ask about real disasters. "I don't want to say" is always OK.
  • After if, use the present: If it rains (not If it will rain). will goes in the other half. In English if needs a subject: If it rains (not If rains).
  • probably goes after will and before won't: It will probably rain. It probably won't snow. Maybe goes at the start: Maybe it will snow.
  • Mixed levels: stronger learners add because to each Ready Plan sentence. Newer learners use Box 1 as a script.
  • Typical mistakes this week: If it will rain, If rains, It will rain probably, It won't probably, You should to buy. Say the right form clearly; the learner repeats. Learners can read the Spanish note and the tip on their Grammar page themselves; you don't need to explain them.

Listen to Lina. She's at the service desk at Valley Mart, a big store.

sections.title: Grammar
sections.html:
Read across. A reads from the left side. B answers from the right side. Choose one part from each column.

Grammar Box 1: Can I help you?

QUESTION
Can I help you?
→
ANSWER
Yes, I'd like toreturn / exchangethis shirt. / these shoes.
Yes, I'd likea refund, / store credit,please.

Grammar Box 2: Reasons

QUESTION
Why? /What's wrong with it?
What's wrong with them?
→
ANSWER (because + a reason)
Because it'stoo small. / too big. / broken.
Because theyhave a stain. / don't fit.

Grammar Box 3: Asking for permission

QUESTION
Could I / Can Iexchange it for a large? / get a refund?
May I (very polite)speak to the manager? / pay with a card?
→
ANSWER
Sure. / Of course.
Sorry, you need the receipt. / Sorry, cash only.

Grammar Box 4: Changing an appointment

CALLER
I'd like tochange my appointment. / reschedule my appointment.
Is Thursdayavailable?
I'd like tocancel my appointment.
→
RECEPTIONIST
What day is good for you?
Yes, at 4:30. / Sorry, we're full. Is Friday OK?
OK. Your appointment is canceled.

Grammar Box 5: I'd like + a thing, I'd like to + a verb

I'd like + A THING
I'd like a refund.
I'd like a bigger size.
I'd like an appointment on Friday.
→
I'd like to + A VERB
I'd like to return this.
I'd like to exchange it.
I'd like to cancel my appointment.

Questions and answers

Q: I'd like or I want?

A: I'd like (= I would like) is more polite. Use it in stores, at the clinic, and on the phone.

Q: I'd like or I'd like to?

A: A thing after I'd like (I'd like a bag). A verb after I'd like to (I'd like to return it).

Q: too small or very small?

A: too small = a problem: it doesn't fit. very small = not a problem. It's too small, so I'd like to exchange it.

Q: Could I, Can I, or May I?

A: All three are OK. May I is the most polite. After them, use the base verb: Could I exchange it? (not to exchange)

Practice A: Write like or like to.

  1. I'd ____________ return these shoes.
  2. I'd ____________ a bag, please.
  3. I'd ____________ exchange this shirt for a medium.
  4. I'd ____________ a refund, please.
  5. I'd ____________ cancel my appointment.

Practice B: Circle the right words.

  1. (Could / Would) I exchange this?
  2. May I (speak / to speak) to the manager?
  3. It's (too small / small too). It doesn't fit.
  4. I'd like to (cancel / canceling) my appointment.
  5. Is Thursday (available / free time)?

Common mistakes

✗ Don't say✓ Say
I'd like return this.I'd like to return this.
I want change my appointment.I'd like to change my appointment.
Could I to exchange it?Could I exchange it?
It's very small. It doesn't fit.It's too small. It doesn't fit.
I'd like to a refund.I'd like a refund.

Nota para hispanohablantes: I'd like to return this = Quisiera devolver esto. return = devolver; exchange = cambiar. May I…? es muy cortés, como ¿Me permite…?

Tip for speakers of other languages: after I'd like use a thing (I'd like a bag). After I'd like to use a verb (I'd like to return it).

lessons.teacher:
How to Use This Plan

You don't need to speak Spanish or any other language. Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. Each Grammar page has one short Spanish note and one tip for speakers of other languages. Learners read them on their own. You never need to read, translate, or explain them.

Instructions: use the same short task words every week: Listen. Circle. Check. Write. Work with a partner. Work in a group. Ask a follow-up question. Learners have the Task Words page from Lesson 1.

Instruction rule: Model it (do it with one learner while everyone watches), check it (ask: "Do you write or speak? How many people do you talk to?"), then go. Say less, show more.

Grouping toolkit: Pairs: turn to a neighbor; with an odd number, make one group of 3. Groups: 3–4 learners. Inside–outside circles: the inner circle faces out, the outer circle faces in; the outer circle moves one person to the right each round. Mingle: everyone stands and talks to many classmates. The teacher joins a pair only if one learner is left over.

When a learner is stuck or speaks another language to you: (1) show it: the picture, a gesture, or the board; (2) give one more short English example; (3) point to the grammar box on their page; (4) a classmate can help for a few seconds, then back to English. You don't need to understand what classmates say to each other.

Lesson 7 (Week 7): Can I Exchange This?

At a glance

Objectives: learners can…

  • say I'd like to return / exchange this and give a reason (because it's too small)
  • ask for permission with Could I / Can I / May I…? and answer
  • ask for a refund or store credit, and ask for the manager politely
  • change or cancel an appointment by phone
  • tell the difference between I'd like + a thing and I'd like to + a verb
  • read a store return policy and fill out a return form

Materials

  • Student Pages for Lesson 7 (print for the number expected + 3 spares)
  • Talk Time: the Store Policy Card, the Customer Cards, and the calendar slips (on the Talk Time pages)
  • phone + small speaker, L3_L7_listening.mp3
  • optional: a T-shirt or a bag to "return" when you model (no play money needed)
  • Prep time: 10 min.

Key vocabulary (with pictures on the New Words page)

★ return • ★ exchange • ★ refund • ★ store credit • ★ size • ★ broken • ★ customer • ★ manager • ★ cancel • ★ reschedule • ★ available • stain

Clock-time plan

Times are loose. If a step runs long, take time from Read & Write first, then from Talk Time.

TimeStepMinGrouping (15 / 7–8)If running behind
6:00–6:10Opening Talk + Homework Check10Pairs (7 pairs + 1 trio / 3–4 pairs)One card only
6:10–6:18New Words (picture page) + pair game8Whole class, then pairsTeach the ★ words only
6:18–6:30Listening: play 1 (Task A), play 2 (Tasks B and C) + "Say it"12Individuals, then pairs checkDo Task C together on the board
6:30–6:45Grammar Q&A: I'd like to…; reasons; Could I / May I…?; appointments + pair drill15Whole class, then pairsSkip the pair drill; Talk Time practices it
6:45–7:00BREAK15
7:00–7:12Talk Time: Service Desk + phone call (back to back)12Pairs (clerk / customer)Round 1 only
7:12–7:17Exit Ticket + Homework5IndividualsNever skip
7:17–7:25Read & Write: a return policy + a return form8Individuals, then pairsReading questions only; the form becomes homework
7:25–7:30Progress Check5IndividualsDo it at the start of the midterm review, while people arrive

Skip order if you're running behind: (1) the Read & Write form (it becomes homework); (2) the pair drill at the end of Grammar; (3) half of Talk Time (Round 1 only). Never skip: the listening tasks, the grammar boxes and the mistakes table, and the exit ticket.

Attendance (15 → 7–8): every step lists both sizes. With 5 or fewer, sit at one table: one "service desk" (one clerk), and customers take turns.

Next week is the midterm (Week 8). Remind learners at the end of class. The midterm reviews Lessons 1–7.

Step by step

Step 1 · 6:00–6:10 · Opening Talk + Homework Check · 10 min

  • Grouping: pairs, the same partner for both parts. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs.
  • Before class: write on the board: What will you do if…? If…, I'll…
  • Opening Talk (6 min): learners open the Opening Talk page. A asks a card question; B answers with 2–3 sentences; A asks one follow-up. Switch after each card.
  • Model with one learner: "What will you do if it rains this weekend?" → (answer) → "Really? With who?"
  • Homework Check (4 min): partners read their Lesson 6 Homework item 1 (If it rains this weekend, I'll…) to each other. Walk around. Write 2 common errors on the board (often If it will rain or If rains) and correct them together.
  • Late arrivals: join any pair as a group of 3.
  • If behind: one card only, then the homework check.

Step 2 · 6:10–6:18 · New Words · 8 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Show the New Words page.
  • Do: point to each picture and say the word. Learners repeat once. Hold up a T-shirt: "It's too small. I'd like to return it… or exchange it for a large."
  • Two pairs of words (1 min): refund (money back) vs. store credit (money for this store only). cancel (no appointment) vs. reschedule (a new day or time).
  • Check meaning (1 min): "The shirt has a brown spot. It has a…?" (stain) • "The phone doesn't work. It's…?" (broken) • "Who is the boss in the store?" (the manager) • "Thursday at 4:30 is free. It's…?" (available)
  • Pairs (2 min): A says a word; B points to the picture and makes a sentence (I'd like a refund.). Switch.
  • If behind: teach the ★ words only.

Step 3 · 6:18–6:30 · Listening + "Say it" · 12 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Before you listen (1 min): point to the customer picture. Say: "This is Lina. She's at the service desk at Valley Mart, a big store. She has a phone case. What does she want to do? Listen."
  • Play 1 → Task A (return or exchange? refund or store credit?). Pairs compare. Check together.
  • Read Tasks B and C together (1 min) so learners know what to listen for.
  • Play 2 → Tasks B and C. Pairs compare. Then show the answers (answer key).
  • "Say it" (2 min): say: "Polite questions go up at the end: Could I exchange it? ↗" Then: "I'd like to is fast: I'd-like-tuh." Read the lines in the "Say it" box. The class repeats each line twice.
  • The audio plays the conversation once (about 1:17). Press play again for play 2. A third play is fine if the class needs it.
  • If behind: do Task C together on the board, reading the lines yourself.

Step 4 · 6:30–6:45 · Grammar Q&A · 15 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Show the Grammar page. The left side is the question. The right side is the answer.
  • Write on the board: I'd like + a thing (I'd like a bag) and I'd like to + a verb (I'd like to return it).
  • Boxes 1 and 2 (4 min): you are the clerk: "Can I help you?" The class answers from Box 1. Then "What's wrong with it?" The class answers from Box 2 (It's too small. It has a stain.).
  • Box 3 (3 min): Could I / Can I / May I…? May I is the most polite. Read the answers: Sure. / Of course. / Sorry, you need the receipt.
  • Box 4 (2 min): appointments. Read the phone lines across with one learner.
  • Check questions: "I'd like ___ return this." (to) • "I'd like ___ refund." (a) • "It's ___ small. It doesn't fit." (too) • "___ I speak to the manager?" (May / Could)
  • Practice A and B (3 min): learners write, then pairs check. Go over the answers.
  • Pair drill (last 2 min): A is the clerk: "Can I help you?" B returns something from the New Words page with a reason. Switch.
  • If behind: skip the pair drill. Talk Time practices it.

Break · 6:45–7:00 · 15 min

  • Write on the board: I'd like to return / exchange this, because… / Could I…? / May I speak to the manager?

Step 5 · 7:00–7:12 · Talk Time: Service Desk · 12 min

  • Grouping: pairs: A = clerk, B = customer. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 trio (two customers wait in line). 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs. 5 or fewer: one clerk; customers take turns.
  • Round 1 (6 min): the clerk reads the Store Policy Card (30 days, receipt needed for a refund, store credit with no receipt, sale items store credit only). The customer chooses a Customer Card and returns or exchanges the item. The clerk follows the policy. After each card, switch roles.
  • Model with one learner (1 min): you are the customer with card 1: "Hi. I'd like to return these shoes." → "What's wrong with them?" → "They're too big." → "Do you have the receipt?" → "Yes, here it is."
  • Round 2, phone call (5 min): pairs sit back to back (no looking). A is the receptionist with the available times. B is the patient and wants to change or cancel an appointment. B uses the calendar slip. Then switch with the second slip.
  • If behind: Round 1 only.

Step 6 · 7:12–7:17 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP

  • Exit ticket: each learner writes two sentences on a slip: one with I'd like to… and a reason with because (I'd like to exchange this shirt, because it has a stain.), and one polite question with Could I or May I. Collect at the door.
  • Homework: open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (one sentence on the board). Say: "About 15 minutes. Bring it next week. Next week is the midterm review."

Read & Write · 7:17–7:25 · A Return Policy and a Return Form · 8 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Read (3 min): learners read the Valley Mart return policy and answer questions 1–5. Say: "Read fast first. Then find the answers."
  • Pairs check (1 min): compare answers; check together.
  • Write (4 min): learners read the situation and fill out the return form. They choose refund, exchange, or store credit (any choice that fits the policy is correct).
  • If behind: questions 1–5 only; the form becomes homework.

Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min

  • Grouping: individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
  • Part A: read the 4 sentences in the answer key, slowly, 2 times each. Learners circle a or b.
  • Parts B and C: learners do them alone. Walk around and help with the instructions only.
  • Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "With a little help." 😐 "Not yet."
  • Collect the pages (or check them at the start of Week 8).
  • If behind: do the Progress Check at the start of the midterm review, while learners arrive.

Listening script: L3_L7_listening.mp3 (about 1:17; the conversation plays once, so press play again for the second listen)

Audio: play from a phone + small speaker. No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer, at a normal, friendly speed.

Narrator: Lesson seven. Listening. Lina is at the service desk at Valley Mart. Listen.

Clerk: Hi. Can I help you?

Lina: Yes, I'd like to return this phone case.

Clerk: OK. What's wrong with it?

Lina: It's too small. It doesn't fit my phone.

Clerk: I see. Do you have the receipt?

Lina: No, sorry. I lost it. Could I get a refund?

Clerk: Sorry, you need the receipt for a refund. But I can give you store credit.

Lina: OK, that's fine. I'd like a bigger case.

Clerk: Sure. The bigger cases are in aisle five.

Lina: Thanks. Also, I have an appointment at your eye center on Monday. I'd like to change it.

Clerk: No problem. I can do that here. What day is good for you?

Lina: Is Thursday available?

Clerk: Let me check. Yes, Thursday at four thirty is available.

Lina: Perfect. I'd like to take that time.

Clerk: OK. Your new appointment is Thursday at four thirty.

Lina: Thank you so much.

Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Answer key

  • Listening Task A: 1 a (return it) • 2 b (store credit; she has no receipt).
  • Listening Task B: 1 too small • 2 Monday • 3 Thursday • 4 4:30.
  • Listening Task C: 1 like to, 2 Could, 3 like, 4 like to, 5 like to.
  • Grammar Practice A: 1 like to, 2 like, 3 like to, 4 like, 5 like to.
  • Grammar Practice B: 1 Could, 2 speak, 3 too small, 4 cancel, 5 available.
  • Talk Time Round 1 (following the Store Policy Card): 1 shoes, too big, receipt, 10 days → refund or exchange • 2 lamp, broken, no receipt → store credit • 3 jacket on sale, stain → store credit only • 4 shirt, 45 days → sorry, more than 30 days (the customer can ask for the manager) • 5 coffee maker, wrong color, receipt, 5 days → refund or exchange • 6 pants, too long, no receipt → store credit or exchange. Wording will vary.
  • Talk Time Round 2: Slip 1: Tuesday 10:00 → a new time on Wednesday or Friday (Wednesday 3:00, Friday 9:30, or Friday 4:30) • Slip 2: cancel the Thursday 2:00 appointment. Answers will vary.
  • Homework 1: answers will vary; for example 1 I'd like to return these shoes, because they're too small. Homework 2: 1 like to, 2 like, 3 like to, 4 like, 5 like to, 6 like to. Homework 3 and 4: answers will vary.
  • Read & Write B: 1 30 days • 2 store credit • 3 No (phones and electronics: 15 days only) • 4 No (no returns on food and medicine) • 5 store credit only
  • Read & Write C (sample form): Item: a blue sweater, size M • Date bought: 10 days ago • Price: $24 • Reason: It has a stain. • Receipt: Yes • I'd like: a refund or an exchange (both fit the policy; store credit is also OK). Wording will vary.
  • Progress Check Part A (the teacher says, 2 times each): 1 "I'd like to return these shoes. They're too big." → a • 2 "Could I exchange this shirt for a large?" → b • 3 "I'd like to cancel my appointment on Friday." → a • 4 "Is Tuesday at ten available? I'd like to change my appointment." → b
  • Progress Check Part B: 1 to return, 2 exchange, 3 too small, 4 a refund.
  • Progress Check Part C: answers will vary; for example 1 I'd like to return this lamp, because it's broken. 2 May I speak to the manager, please?
  • Progress Check scoring: A /4 + B /4 + C /2 = /10. This is not a test grade. It shows who needs more help hearing requests (A) and with I'd like / I'd like to and polite questions (B, C).

Teacher notes

  • Invented stores only (important): Valley Mart, its policy, and the eye center are invented. No play money is needed. Learners never talk about their own purchases, debts, or money problems.
  • I'd like vs. I'd like to: after I'd like, use a thing (I'd like a bag). After I'd like to, use a verb (I'd like to return it). I'd like = I would like: more polite than I want.
  • too + adjective: It's too small means it's a problem (it doesn't fit). very small is not a problem. Teach too small / too big / too long as fixed phrases.
  • Could I / Can I / May I: all are OK. May I is the most polite and formal. The answer is usually Sure. / Of course. / Sorry, ….
  • Midterm next week: remind learners. The midterm reviews Lessons 1–7.
  • Mixed levels: stronger learners argue politely in Round 1 (Could I speak to the manager, please?). Newer learners use Boxes 1–3 as a script.
  • Typical mistakes this week: I'd like return, I like to return this (for now), Could I to exchange, It's very small (for a problem), I want change my appointment. Say the right form clearly; the learner repeats. Learners can read the Spanish note and the tip on their Grammar page themselves; you don't need to explain them.

sections.html:
Read across. A reads from the left side. B answers from the right side. Choose one part from each column.

Grammar Box 1: Whose…?

QUESTION
Whoseumbrella / walletis this?
Whosekeys / glovesare these?
Whosebackpackis that?
→
ANSWER
It'smine. / hers. / Ana's.
They'reours. / his. / Tom's.
I think it'stheirs. / yours.

Grammar Box 2: Is this yours?

QUESTION
Is thisyours? / his?
Are theseyours? / theirs?
→
ANSWER
Yes, it's mine. / Yes, it's his.Thank you!
No, it isn't mine.Maybe it's hers.
No, they aren't ours.Ours are black.

Grammar Box 3: my bag → mine

+ A NOUNNO NOUN+ A NOUNNO NOUN
It's my bag.It's mine.It's her bag.It's hers.
It's your bag.It's yours.It's our bag.It's ours.
It's his bag.It's his.It's their bag.It's theirs.

Grammar Box 4: Describing an item

SIZECOLORITEMDETAIL
It's asmall / bigblack / bluewallet. / backpack.with a zipper. / with two pockets.
They're—brown / redgloves. / sunglasses.with a star. / in a black case.

Questions and answers

Q: my or mine?

A: my + a noun: It's my bag. mine alone: It's mine. (not It's mine bag)

Q: Can I say It's the mine?

A: No. No the: It's mine. It's hers. And no apostrophe: yours, hers, ours, theirs.

Q: his or hers?

A: his = a man's. hers = a woman's. It's Maria's. It's hers.

Q: Whose or who's?

A: They sound the same. Whose = which person owns it: Whose bag is this? Who's = who is: Who's that?

Q: How do I describe it?

A: Size → color → item → with…: a small black wallet with a zipper (not a wallet black small).

Practice A: Write mine, yours, his, hers, ours, or theirs.

  1. This is my bag. It's ____________.
  2. That's her umbrella. It's ____________.
  3. These are our keys. They're ____________.
  4. Is this your scarf? Is it ____________?
  5. Those are their gloves. They're ____________.
  6. That's his wallet. It's ____________.

Practice B: Circle the right words.

  1. (Whose / Who's) bag is this?
  2. It's (my / mine).
  3. Is this (your / yours) umbrella?
  4. Those sunglasses are (her / hers).
  5. It's a (black small / small black) wallet.

Common mistakes

✗ Don't say✓ Say
It's the mine.It's mine.
Is this your?Is this yours?
Who's bag is this?Whose bag is this?
It's a wallet black.It's a black wallet.

Nota para hispanohablantes: mine = (el / la) mío / mía, pero en inglés no se usa the: It's mine (no It's the mine). His (de él) y hers (de ella) son palabras diferentes; en español suyo sirve para los dos.

Tip for speakers of other languages: mine, yours, hers stand alone. my, your, her need a noun (my bag).

lessons.teacher:
How to Use This Plan

You don't need to speak Spanish or any other language. Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. Each Grammar page has one short Spanish note and one tip for speakers of other languages. Learners read them on their own. You never need to read, translate, or explain them.

Instructions: use the same short task words every week: Listen. Circle. Check. Write. Work with a partner. Work in a group. Ask a follow-up question. Learners have the Task Words page from Lesson 1.

Instruction rule: Model it (do it with one learner while everyone watches), check it (ask: "Do you write or speak? How many people do you talk to?"), then go. Say less, show more.

Grouping toolkit: Pairs: turn to a neighbor; with an odd number, make one group of 3. Groups: 3–4 learners. Inside–outside circles: the inner circle faces out, the outer circle faces in; the outer circle moves one person to the right each round. Mingle: everyone stands and talks to many classmates. The teacher joins a pair only if one learner is left over.

When a learner is stuck or speaks another language to you: (1) show it: the picture, a gesture, or the board; (2) give one more short English example; (3) point to the grammar box on their page; (4) a classmate can help for a few seconds, then back to English. You don't need to understand what classmates say to each other.

Lesson 8 (Week 9): Lost and Found

At a glance

Objectives: learners can…

  • ask Whose… is this? / Whose… are these?
  • answer with mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs or a name + 's (It's Ana's.)
  • ask and answer Is this yours? → Yes, it's mine. / No, it isn't mine.
  • describe a lost item: size, color, and details (a small black wallet with a zipper)
  • say what they were doing when they lost something (I was waiting for the bus when I lost it.)
  • read a FOUND notice, fill out a lost-item report, and write a short FOUND notice

Materials

  • Student Pages for Lesson 8 (print for the number expected + 3 spares)
  • Talk Time: the Lost and Found picture and the Owner Cards (on the Talk Time pages)
  • phone + small speaker, L3_L8_listening.mp3
  • optional: 3 classroom things (a pen, a cup, a book) to show mine / yours / hers
  • Prep time: 10 min.

Key vocabulary (with pictures on the New Words page)

★ wallet • ★ purse • ★ keys • ★ umbrella • ★ backpack • ★ sunglasses • ★ headphones • ★ gloves • ★ scarf • ★ lost and found • ★ belong to • describe

Clock-time plan

Times are loose. If a step runs long, take time from Read & Write first, then from Talk Time.

TimeStepMinGrouping (15 / 7–8)If running behind
6:00–6:10Opening Talk + Midterm check-in10Pairs (7 pairs + 1 trio / 3–4 pairs)One card only
6:10–6:18New Words (picture page) + pair game8Whole class, then pairsTeach the ★ words only
6:18–6:30Listening: play 1 (Task A), play 2 (Tasks B and C) + "Say it"12Individuals, then pairs checkDo Task C together on the board
6:30–6:45Grammar Q&A: Whose…?; mine / yours / his / hers / ours / theirs; describing + pair drill15Whole class, then pairsSkip the pair drill; Talk Time practices it
6:45–7:00BREAK15
7:00–7:12Talk Time: The Lost and Found Box + whose is it?12Pairs, then groups of 3–4Round 1 only
7:12–7:17Exit Ticket + Homework5IndividualsNever skip
7:17–7:25Read & Write: a FOUND notice + a lost-item report; write a FOUND notice8Individuals, then pairsReading questions only; the notice becomes homework
7:25–7:30Progress Check5IndividualsDo it in Week 10 at 6:00, while people arrive

Skip order if you're running behind: (1) the Read & Write FOUND notice (it becomes homework); (2) the pair drill at the end of Grammar; (3) half of Talk Time (Round 1 only). Never skip: the listening tasks, the grammar boxes and the mistakes table, and the exit ticket.

Attendance (15 → 7–8): every step lists both sizes. With 5 or fewer, sit at one table: one clerk, and the others are owners; take turns being the clerk.

Step by step

Step 1 · 6:00–6:10 · Opening Talk + Midterm check-in · 10 min

  • Grouping: pairs, the same partner for both parts. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs.
  • Before class: write on the board: I'd like to… / Could I…? / May I…?
  • Opening Talk (6 min): learners open the Opening Talk page. A asks a card question; B answers with 2–3 sentences; A asks one follow-up. Switch after each card.
  • Model with one learner: "What did you do last weekend?" → (answer) → "Really? How was it?"
  • Midterm check-in (4 min): give back the midterms (if they are marked). Partners say one thing that was easy and one thing that was hard (The listening was easy. Part C was hard, because…). Write 2 common errors from the midterm on the board and correct them together.
  • Late arrivals: join any pair as a group of 3.
  • If behind: one card only, then the check-in.

Step 2 · 6:10–6:18 · New Words · 8 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Show the New Words page.
  • Do: point to each picture and say the word. Learners repeat once. Put on imaginary gloves and a scarf; look for your keys in your pockets: "Where are my keys? I lost them!"
  • Show belong to: hold up your own pen. "This pen belongs to me. It's mine." Point to a learner's book (don't take it): "That book belongs to you. It's yours."
  • Check meaning (1 min): "Where do you keep money?" (a wallet / a purse) • "You listen to music with…?" (headphones) • "At the bus station, where do they keep lost things?" (the lost and found)
  • Pairs (2 min): A says a word; B points to the picture and makes a sentence (My umbrella is black.). Switch.
  • If behind: teach the ★ words only.

Step 3 · 6:18–6:30 · Listening + "Say it" · 12 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Before you listen (1 min): say: "David lost something on the bus. He's calling the lost and found. What did he lose? Listen."
  • Play 1 → Task A (what did he lose?). Pairs compare. Check together.
  • Read Tasks B and C together (1 min) so learners know what to listen for.
  • Play 2 → Tasks B and C. Pairs compare. Then show the answers (answer key).
  • "Say it" (2 min): say: "yours, hers, ours, theirs end with a z sound." Read them; the class repeats. Then: "Whose and who's sound the same: hooz." Read the line in the "Say it" box. The class repeats each line twice.
  • The audio plays the conversation once (about 1:17). Press play again for play 2. A third play is fine if the class needs it.
  • If behind: do Task C together on the board, reading the lines yourself.

Step 4 · 6:30–6:45 · Grammar Q&A · 15 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Show the Grammar page. The left side is the question. The right side is the answer.
  • Show it (2 min): put three things on your desk: your pen, a cup, a book. Point to the pen: "Whose pen is this? It's my pen. It's mine." Give the cup to a woman: "It's her cup. It's hers." Give the book to a man: "It's his."
  • Boxes 1 and 2 (4 min): read a question from the left; the class answers from the right. Point out is this / are these (one / more than one).
  • Box 3 (2 min): read across: my bag → mine. In each pair, the first column needs a noun; the second stands alone.
  • Box 4 (2 min): describing: size → color → item → with… Hold up something: "It's a small blue pen with a cap."
  • Check questions: "This is my book. It's ___." (mine) • "___ keys are these?" (Whose) • "It's her umbrella. It's ___." (hers) • "a ___ wallet: black / small" (small black)
  • Practice A and B (3 min): learners write, then pairs check. Go over the answers.
  • Pair drill (last 2 min): A points to something in a picture on the New Words page: "Whose ___ is this?" B answers with a pronoun or a classmate's name + 's. Switch.
  • If behind: skip the pair drill. Talk Time practices it.

Break · 6:45–7:00 · 15 min

  • Write on the board: Whose… is this? / Is this yours? / It's mine. / It isn't mine. Maybe it's hers. and size → color → item → with…

Step 5 · 7:00–7:12 · Talk Time: The Lost and Found Box · 12 min

  • Grouping: Round 1 pairs (A = clerk, B = owner); Round 2 groups of 3–4. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 trio. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs. 5 or fewer: one clerk, the others are owners.
  • Round 1 (7 min): each owner takes an Owner Card (the teacher gives one number, 1–8; use the cards in order). The owner fills in the short lost-item form on the card (small, red, backpack…). Then the owner describes the item to the clerk. The clerk looks at the Lost and Found picture and asks Is this yours? (pointing to a number). The owner answers: Yes, it's mine! / No, it isn't mine. Mine is… Then switch with a new card.
  • Model with one learner (1 min): you are the owner with card 1: "I lost my backpack. It's big and blue." The learner points: "Is number 1 yours?" → "Yes, it's mine! Thank you!"
  • Round 2, groups (4 min): each person keeps their last Owner Card. The group looks at the picture together and says whose each item is: Number 3 is Maria's. It's hers. Number 9 is mine. If no one has the card, say It isn't ours. Maybe it's theirs (another group's).
  • If behind: Round 1 only.

Step 6 · 7:12–7:17 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP

  • Exit ticket: each learner writes two sentences on a slip: one with a possessive pronoun (This umbrella isn't mine. It's hers.), and one about losing something with when and because or so (I was waiting for the bus when I lost my keys, so I called the lost and found.). Collect at the door.
  • Homework: open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (one sentence on the board). Say: "About 15 minutes. Bring it next week."

Read & Write · 7:17–7:25 · A FOUND Notice and a Lost-Item Report · 8 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Read (3 min): learners read the FOUND notice and the lost-item report and answer questions 1–5. Say: "Read fast first. Then find the answers."
  • Pairs check (1 min): compare answers; check together.
  • Write (4 min): learners choose one item from the Lost and Found picture and write a short FOUND notice (what, where, when, how to contact). Say: "Invent a first name and use a 555 phone number."
  • If behind: questions 1–5 only; the notice becomes homework.

Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min

  • Grouping: individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
  • Part A: read the 4 sentences in the answer key, slowly, 2 times each. Learners circle a or b.
  • Parts B and C: learners do them alone. Walk around and help with the instructions only.
  • Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "With a little help." 😐 "Not yet."
  • Collect the pages (or check them at the start of Week 10).
  • If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 10 at 6:00, while learners arrive.

Listening script: L3_L8_listening.mp3 (about 1:17; the conversation plays once, so press play again for the second listen)

Audio: play from a phone + small speaker. No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer, at a normal, friendly speed.

Narrator: Lesson eight. Listening. David lost something on the bus. He's calling the lost and found. Listen.

Joan: City Bus, Lost and Found. How can I help you?

David: Hi. I lost my backpack on the bus this morning.

Joan: OK. Can you describe it?

David: It's a big blue backpack with a black zipper. My brother has the same one, but his is green.

Joan: What was inside?

David: My headphones, a red scarf, and some gloves.

Joan: And what were you doing when you lost it?

David: I was talking on the phone. I got off at Park Street, and I left it on the seat.

Joan: Let me check. We have two blue backpacks. One is small, and one is big.

David: The big one is mine.

Joan: There are white headphones inside. Are they yours?

David: No, mine are black. Those aren't mine.

Joan: Wait. Here's another big one, with black headphones and a red scarf.

David: Yes! That's mine. Thank you!

Joan: You're welcome. You can pick it up today before five.

Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Answer key

  • Listening Task A: b (a backpack).
  • Listening Task B: 1 blue • 2 big • 3 ✓ headphones, ✓ a scarf, ✓ gloves, ✗ a wallet, ✗ keys • 4 Park Street • 5 5:00.
  • Listening Task C: 1 his, 2 mine, 3 yours, 4 mine, 5 mine.
  • Grammar Practice A: 1 mine, 2 hers, 3 ours, 4 yours, 5 theirs, 6 his.
  • Grammar Practice B: 1 Whose, 2 mine, 3 your, 4 hers, 5 small black.
  • Talk Time Round 1 (Owner Card → picture number): 1 → 1 (big blue backpack) • 2 → 4 (red umbrella) • 3 → 6 (keys with a heart) • 4 → 10 (brown wallet) • 5 → 12 (green scarf) • 6 → 8 (glasses with blue lenses) • 7 → 2 (small red backpack) • 8 → 9 (black wallet). Items 3, 5, 7, and 11 have no owner. Round 2: answers will vary.
  • Homework 1: 1 It's mine. 2 They're hers. 3 It's ours. 4 Are they yours? Homework 2: answers will vary (size → color → item → with…). Homework 3 and 4: answers will vary.
  • Read & Write B: 1 keys (a set of keys with a blue star key chain) • 2 at Lincoln Park, near the basketball courts • 3 on Saturday, May 9 • 4 describe the key chain and say where you lost them • 5 a black umbrella with a wooden handle • Writing (C): answers will vary.
  • Progress Check Part A (the teacher says, 2 times each): 1 "Whose keys are these? They're mine." → a • 2 "Is this your umbrella? No, it's hers." → b • 3 "I lost a small black wallet." → a • 4 "These gloves aren't ours. They're theirs." → b
  • Progress Check Part B: 1 Whose, 2 mine, 3 Their, 4 yours.
  • Progress Check Part C: answers will vary; for example 1 I lost a big red backpack with a zipper. 2 It's mine. / It's Ana's.
  • Progress Check scoring: A /4 + B /4 + C /2 = /10. This is not a test grade. It shows who needs more help hearing possessives (A) and with the forms (B, C).

Teacher notes

  • Picture cards, not real things (important): use the pictures and Owner Cards, not learners' real wallets, purses, or phones. Remind learners never to write real ID numbers, bank card numbers, or addresses on any form, in class or in real life on a public notice.
  • Two kinds of words: my, your, his, her, our, their need a noun (my bag). mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs stand alone (It's mine). his is the same in both.
  • No the: It's mine (not It's the mine). No apostrophe: yours, hers, ours, theirs (not your's).
  • Whose and who's: they sound the same. Whose = which person owns it (Whose bag is this?). Who's = who is (Who's that?).
  • Describing order: size → color → item → with… (a small black wallet with a zipper). Don't teach a long rule; this one order is enough.
  • Typical mistakes this week: It's the mine, Is this your?, Who's bag is this?, It's mine bag, a wallet black, his for a woman (It's Maria's. It's his.). Say the right form clearly; the learner repeats. Learners can read the Spanish note and the tip on their Grammar page themselves; you don't need to explain them.
  • Mixed levels: stronger learners add when and where they lost the item with the past continuous. Newer learners use Boxes 1 and 2 as a script.

sections.html:
Read across. A reads from the left side. B answers from the right side. Choose one part from each column.

Grammar Box 1: good at

QUESTION
What are yougood at?
Are yougood at organizing?
Are yougood with people?
→
ANSWER
I'm good atfixing things. / cooking.
Yes, I am. I'm good atorganizing shelves.
Yes, I'm good withpeople. / numbers. / my hands.

Grammar Box 2: interested in

QUESTION
What are youinterested in?
Are youinterested in training?
→
ANSWER
I'm interested inlearning new skills.
Yes, I'm very interested inworking with computers.

Grammar Box 3: enjoy / don't mind

QUESTION
Do youenjoy working on a team?
Can youwork weekends?
→
ANSWER
Yes, I enjoyhelping people.
Yes, I don't mindworking weekends. / working at night.

Grammar Box 4: -ing spelling

MOST VERBS: + -ingEND IN e: no e + -ingSHORT WORDS: double + -ing
fix → fixingorganize → organizingshop → shopping
help → helpingsolve → solvingrun → running
work → workingdrive → drivingplan → planning

Questions and answers

Q: good at fix or good at fixing?

A: good at fixing. After at, in, about, use -ing. (not good at fix)

Q: interested in or interested on?

A: interested in: I'm interested in learning English.

Q: I enjoy to work or I enjoy working?

A: I enjoy working. After enjoy and don't mind, use -ing.

Q: good at or good with?

A: good at + an activity: good at cooking. good with + people or things: good with people, good with numbers.

Q: What does I don't mind mean?

A: It's OK for me. It's not a problem: I don't mind working weekends.

Practice A: Write the -ing word.

  1. I'm good at ____________ (cook).
  2. She's interested in ____________ (learn) English.
  3. Do you enjoy ____________ (work) outside?
  4. He's good at ____________ (organize) things.
  5. They don't mind ____________ (shop) for the office.
  6. I'm good at ____________ (fix) bikes.

Practice B: Circle the right words.

  1. I'm good (at / in) solving problems.
  2. Are you interested (on / in) training?
  3. I enjoy (help / helping) customers.
  4. I don't mind (work / working) at night.
  5. She's (good at / good with) people.

Common mistakes

✗ Don't say✓ Say
I'm good at cook.I'm good at cooking.
I'm interested on computers.I'm interested in computers.
I enjoy to work on a team.I enjoy working on a team.
I don't mind work weekends.I don't mind working weekends.

Nota para hispanohablantes: después de at / in / about, el inglés usa -ing: good at cooking (en español: bueno para cocinar, con el infinitivo). Se dice interested in (no interested on).

Tip for speakers of other languages: in an interview, give an example after each strength: I'm reliable. I was never late at my last job.
