lessons.teacher:
How to Use This Plan

You don't need to speak Spanish or any other language. Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. Each Grammar page has one short Spanish note and one tip for speakers of other languages. Learners read them on their own. You never need to read, translate, or explain them.

Instructions: use the same short task words every week: Listen. Circle. Check. Write. Work with a partner. Work in a group. Ask a follow-up question. Learners have the Task Words page from Lesson 1.

Instruction rule: Model it (do it with one learner while everyone watches), check it (ask: "Do you write or speak? How many people do you talk to?"), then go. Say less, show more.

Grouping toolkit: Pairs: turn to a neighbor; with an odd number, make one group of 3. Groups: 3–4 learners. Inside–outside circles: the inner circle faces out, the outer circle faces in; the outer circle moves one person to the right each round. Mingle: everyone stands and talks to many classmates. The teacher joins a pair only if one learner is left over.

When a learner is stuck or speaks another language to you: (1) show it: the picture, a gesture, or the board; (2) give one more short English example; (3) point to the grammar box on their page; (4) a classmate can help for a few seconds, then back to English. You don't need to understand what classmates say to each other.

Lesson 9 (Week 10): My Strengths

At a glance

Objectives: learners can…

  • say what they are good at: I'm good at fixing things. / I'm good with people.
  • say what they are interested in: I'm interested in learning new skills.
  • say what they enjoy and don't mind: I enjoy helping people. I don't mind working weekends.
  • give an example after a strength: I'm reliable. I was never late at my last job.
  • answer Tell me about yourself in 3–4 sentences
  • read two short job ads and write a 3-sentence skills summary

Materials

  • Student Pages for Lesson 9 (print for the number expected + 3 spares)
  • Talk Time: the four job cards and the Manager Questions (on the Talk Time pages)
  • phone + small speaker, L3_L9_listening.mp3
  • Prep time: 10 min (decide where the two circles will stand).

Key vocabulary (with pictures on the New Words page)

★ strength • ★ good at • ★ interested in • ★ experience • ★ reliable • ★ teamwork • ★ organize • ★ solve problems • ★ résumé • ★ apply • ★ training • shift

Clock-time plan

Times are loose. If a step runs long, take time from Read & Write first, then from Talk Time.

TimeStepMinGrouping (15 / 7–8)If running behind
6:00–6:10Opening Talk + Homework Check10Pairs (7 pairs + 1 trio / 3–4 pairs)One card only
6:10–6:18New Words (picture page) + pair game8Whole class, then pairsTeach the ★ words only
6:18–6:30Listening: play 1 (Task A), play 2 (Tasks B and C) + "Say it"12Individuals, then pairs checkDo Task C together on the board
6:30–6:45Grammar Q&A: good at / interested in / enjoy / don't mind + -ing + pair drill15Whole class, then pairsSkip the pair drill; Talk Time practices it
6:45–7:00BREAK15
7:00–7:12Talk Time: Interview Rotation12Inside–outside circles (pairs with 5 or fewer)2 rotations, no role switch
7:12–7:17Exit Ticket + Homework5IndividualsNever skip
7:17–7:25Read & Write: two job ads; write a skills summary8Individuals, then pairsReading questions only; the summary becomes homework
7:25–7:30Progress Check5IndividualsDo it in Week 11 at 6:00, while people arrive

Skip order if you're running behind: (1) the Read & Write skills summary (it becomes homework); (2) the pair drill at the end of Grammar; (3) half of Talk Time (2 rotations, no role switch). Never skip: the listening tasks, the grammar boxes and the mistakes table, and the exit ticket.

Attendance (15 → 7–8): every step lists both sizes. With 5 or fewer, sit at one table: one manager interviews one applicant while the others listen and note one strength; then change roles.

Step by step

Step 1 · 6:00–6:10 · Opening Talk + Homework Check · 10 min

  • Grouping: pairs, the same partner for both parts. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs.
  • Before class: write on the board: Whose… is this? It's mine. / It's hers.
  • Opening Talk (6 min): learners open the Opening Talk page. A asks a card question; B answers with 2–3 sentences; A asks one follow-up. Switch after each card.
  • Model with one learner: "Did you ever lose something important?" → (answer) → "Really? Where did you find it?"
  • Homework Check (4 min): partners read their Lesson 8 Homework item 3 (The blue cup is mine…) to each other. Walk around. Write 2 common errors on the board (often It's the mine or his for a woman) and correct them together.
  • Late arrivals: join any pair as a group of 3.
  • If behind: one card only, then the homework check.

Step 2 · 6:10–6:18 · New Words · 8 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Show the New Words page.
  • Do: point to each picture and say the word. Learners repeat once. Show strength: make a strong arm. Show reliable: point to the clock, "always on time."
  • Show good at: "I'm good at cooking. I'm not good at singing!" Mime both.
  • Check meaning (1 min): "A paper with your jobs and skills is a…?" (résumé) • "Morning, evening, or night work time is a…?" (shift) • "A class at work for new workers is…?" (training)
  • Pairs (2 min): A says a word; B points to the picture and makes a sentence (I'm good at solving problems.). Switch.
  • If behind: teach the ★ words only.

Step 3 · 6:18–6:30 · Listening + "Say it" · 12 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Before you listen (1 min): say: "Lucia has a job interview at a hotel. She wants a maintenance job. Does she get a second interview? Listen."
  • Play 1 → Task A (a second interview?). Pairs compare. Check together.
  • Read Tasks B and C together (1 min) so learners know what to listen for.
  • Play 2 → Tasks B and C. Pairs compare. Then show the answers (answer key).
  • "Say it" (2 min): say: "The end of -ing is in the nose: fix-ing, help-ing, work-ing." Don't add a g or k sound at the end. Then stress: INterested, exPERience. The class repeats each word twice.
  • The audio plays the conversation once (about 1:20). Press play again for play 2. A third play is fine if the class needs it.
  • If behind: do Task C together on the board, reading the lines yourself.

Step 4 · 6:30–6:45 · Grammar Q&A · 15 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Show the Grammar page. The left side is the question. The right side is the answer.
  • Show it (2 min): write on the board: good at + fixing. Say: "After at, in, about, the verb gets -ing." Write I'm good at fix. and cross it out.
  • Boxes 1, 2, and 3 (5 min): read a question from the left; the class answers from the right. Then ask 3 learners: "What are you good at?" Help them finish with an -ing word.
  • Box 4 (2 min): read the spelling rows: fix → fixing, organize → organizing (no e), shop → shopping (double letter).
  • Check questions: "I'm interested ___ learning." (in) • "I enjoy ___ (help) people." (helping) • "I'm good ___ cooking." (at) • "I don't mind ___ (work) at night." (working)
  • Practice A and B (3 min): learners write, then pairs check. Go over the answers.
  • Pair drill (last 2 min): A asks "What are you good at?" B answers and gives one example (I'm good at cooking. I cook for my family every day.). Switch.
  • If behind: skip the pair drill. Talk Time practices it.

Break · 6:45–7:00 · 15 min

  • Write on the board: What are you good at? / Are you interested in…? / Do you enjoy…? / I don't mind… and at / in + -ing. Set up the two circles of chairs if you have the space.

Step 5 · 7:00–7:12 · Talk Time: Interview Rotation · 12 min

  • Grouping: inside–outside circles. The inner circle are managers; the outer circle are applicants. 15 learners: 7 managers + 8 applicants (one applicant waits and listens each round). 7–8 learners: 4 and 4 (or 3 and 4). 5 or fewer: one manager, the others take turns as applicants.
  • Before (2 min): each manager chooses a job card (1–4) and the Manager Questions. Each applicant fills in the "My answers" box on their page (strengths, experience, shifts). Invented details are fine.
  • Model with one learner (1 min): you are the manager at the hotel (card 2). "Tell me about yourself." → (answer) → "What are you good at?" → (answer) → follow-up: "Can you give me an example?"
  • Rotation (6 min): each interview is about 2 minutes: the manager asks 3 questions from the card and one follow-up, then writes one strength in the notes table. Then say "Move!" The outer circle moves one person to the right. 3 rotations.
  • Switch (3 min): managers and applicants change places for one or two more rotations.
  • Finish: ask 2 managers: "Who gets a second interview? Why?" (Ana, because she's good at organizing.)
  • If behind: 2 rotations, no role switch.

Step 6 · 7:12–7:17 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP

  • Exit ticket: each learner writes two sentences on a slip: one with good at or interested in + -ing (I'm good at organizing things.), and one with an example and because or so (I'm reliable, so I'm never late.). Collect at the door.
  • Homework: open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (one sentence on the board). Say: "About 15 minutes. Bring it next week."

Read & Write · 7:17–7:25 · Two Job Ads and a Skills Summary · 8 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Read (3 min): learners read the two job ads and answer questions 1–5. Say: "Read fast first. Then find the answers."
  • Pairs check (1 min): compare answers; check together.
  • Write (4 min): learners write a 3-sentence skills summary for themselves or an invented person: a strength with an example, experience, and an interest. Say: "You can invent the job history."
  • If behind: questions 1–5 only; the summary becomes homework.

Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min

  • Grouping: individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
  • Part A: read the 4 sentences in the answer key, slowly, 2 times each. Learners circle a or b.
  • Parts B and C: learners do them alone. Walk around and help with the instructions only.
  • Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "With a little help." 😐 "Not yet."
  • Collect the pages (or check them at the start of Week 11).
  • If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 11 at 6:00, while learners arrive.

Listening script: L3_L9_listening.mp3 (about 1:20; the conversation plays once, so press play again for the second listen)

Audio: play from a phone + small speaker. No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer, at a normal, friendly speed.

Narrator: Lesson nine. Listening. Lucia has a job interview at a hotel. Mr. Hall is the manager. Listen.

Mr. Hall: Hi, Lucia. Thank you for coming in. Please sit down. So, tell me about yourself.

Lucia: Well, I have three years of experience in maintenance. I worked at a big apartment building.

Mr. Hall: That's great. What are you good at?

Lucia: I'm good at fixing things, and I'm good at solving problems.

Mr. Hall: Are you reliable?

Lucia: Yes. I was never late at my last job, and I always finish my work.

Mr. Hall: Good. Do you enjoy working on a team?

Lucia: Yes, I enjoy helping people. I like teamwork.

Mr. Hall: Are you interested in training? We have a class for new workers.

Lucia: Yes! I'm very interested in learning about the machines here.

Mr. Hall: Which shift can you work?

Lucia: I can work the day shift. And I don't mind working weekends.

Mr. Hall: Great. I'd like you to meet our team. Can you come back on Thursday for a second interview?

Lucia: Yes, of course. Thank you!

Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Answer key

  • Listening Task A: Yes (on Thursday).
  • Listening Task B: 1 three years • 2 ✓ fixing things, ✓ solving problems, ✓ helping people, ✗ cooking, ✗ driving • 3 the day shift • 4 Yes, she doesn't mind working weekends. • 5 Thursday.
  • Listening Task C: 1 fixing, 2 solving, 3 working, 4 helping, 5 learning, 6 working.
  • Grammar Practice A: 1 cooking, 2 learning, 3 working, 4 organizing, 5 shopping, 6 fixing.
  • Grammar Practice B: 1 at, 2 in, 3 helping, 4 working, 5 good with.
  • Talk Time: answers will vary.
  • Homework 1: 1 I'm good at cooking. 2 She's interested in learning English. 3 He enjoys working with his hands. 4 I don't mind working at night. Homework 2, 3, and 4: answers will vary.
  • Read & Write B: 1 Lakeview Inn and Little Stars Center • 2 Little Stars Center • 3 the night shift (11 p.m.–7 a.m.) • 4 a résumé • 5 on Saturday mornings • Writing (C): answers will vary.
  • Progress Check Part A (the teacher says, 2 times each): 1 "He's good at fixing cars." → a • 2 "She's interested in working with children." → b • 3 "He doesn't mind working at night." → a • 4 "He enjoys cooking for his family." → b
  • Progress Check Part B: 1 at, 2 in, 3 working, 4 helping.
  • Progress Check Part C: answers will vary; for example 1 I'm good at organizing. I organize the shelves at my job. 2 I'm interested in learning about computers.
  • Progress Check scoring: A /4 + B /4 + C /2 = /10. This is not a test grade. It shows who needs more help hearing the phrases (A) and with at / in + -ing (B, C).

Teacher notes

  • Invented job histories are fine (important): invite, don't require, real job details. Learners can talk about home, family, or volunteer work, or invent a job history. Never ask about immigration or work status, papers, or pay.
  • The one rule: after at, in, about (and after enjoy and don't mind), use -ing: good at fixing, interested in learning, enjoy helping, don't mind working.
  • good at or good with? good at + an activity (good at cooking). good with + people or things (good with people, good with numbers, good with my hands).
  • Give an example: in a real interview, a strength is stronger with an example: I'm reliable. I was never late at my last job. Praise every example.
  • Spelling: most verbs add -ing. Drop a final e (organize → organizing). Short words like shop, run double the last letter (shopping, running). Don't teach more rules than this.
  • Typical mistakes this week: I'm good at cook, interested on, I enjoy to work, I'm boring of… (save bored / boring for Lesson 11), I don't mind work. Say the right form clearly; the learner repeats. Learners can read the Spanish note and the tip on their Grammar page themselves; you don't need to explain them.
  • Mixed levels: stronger learners add a second example and a follow-up question. Newer learners use Boxes 1–3 as a script.

QUESTION

Next,add the detergent.

Grammar Box 3: Don't…

ANSWER

Don't forget totake your card.

Grammar Box 4: Sequence words

STEP 1STEP 2STEP 3LAST STEP
First, …Next, …Then, … / After that, …Finally, …
First, put on your goggles.Next, fill the tank.Then, plug it in.Finally, turn it off.

Questions and answers

Q: Do I say you in an instruction?

A: No. Start with the verb: Press START. (not You press START)

Q: Press or Presses?

A: Press. Instructions have no -s: Turn it on. Add the soap.

Q: How do I say no in an instruction?

A: Don't + verb: Don't open the door. (not No open)

Q: Don't forget take or Don't forget to take?

A: Don't forget to take your card.

Q: Finally or Final?

A: Finally, for the last step: Finally, turn it off.

Practice A: Write First, Next, Then, After that, or Finally.

Making tea:

  1. ____________, boil the water.
  2. ____________, put a tea bag in the cup.
  3. ____________, add the hot water.
  4. ____________, wait 3 minutes.
  5. ____________, take out the tea bag and drink it.

Practice B: Circle the right words.

  1. (Press / You presses) the green button.
  2. (No open / Don't open) the door.
  3. How (do / does) I log in?
  4. Don't forget (take / to take) your receipt.
  5. (Turn off / Turns off) the light, please.

Common mistakes

✗ Don't say✓ Say
You press START.Press START.
No open the door.Don't open the door.
Don't forget take your card.Don't forget to take your card.
Final, turn it off.Finally, turn it off.

Nota para hispanohablantes: las instrucciones en inglés no tienen you ni terminación: Press START (no You press ni Presses). Negativo: Don't + verbo: Don't open.

Tip for speakers of other languages: listen for the sequence words. They tell you when a new step starts.

sections.title: Homework
sections.html:
Homework (about 15 minutes). Bring it next week!

1. Write the instruction. No you, no -s.

Example: You turn on the light. → Turn on the light.

  1. You press START. → ______________________________________________
  2. You no open the door. → ______________________________________________
  3. You plugs in the machine. → ______________________________________________
  4. Don't forget take your card. → ______________________________________________

2. Write 4 steps for something you do at home (making rice, washing the dishes, doing laundry). Use First, Next, Then, Finally.

Example: First, put the clothes in the machine. Next, add the detergent. Then, press START. Finally, put the clothes in the dryer.

3. Ask a family member or a coworker: How do you make your favorite food? Write 3 steps.

4. Review (Lesson 9): Write 2 sentences about you with good at, interested in, or enjoy + -ing.

lessons.teacher:
How to Use This Plan

You don't need to speak Spanish or any other language. Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. Each Grammar page has one short Spanish note and one tip for speakers of other languages. Learners read them on their own. You never need to read, translate, or explain them.

Instructions: use the same short task words every week: Listen. Circle. Check. Write. Work with a partner. Work in a group. Ask a follow-up question. Learners have the Task Words page from Lesson 1.

Instruction rule: Model it (do it with one learner while everyone watches), check it (ask: "Do you write or speak? How many people do you talk to?"), then go. Say less, show more.

Grouping toolkit: Pairs: turn to a neighbor; with an odd number, make one group of 3. Groups: 3–4 learners. Inside–outside circles: the inner circle faces out, the outer circle faces in; the outer circle moves one person to the right each round. Mingle: everyone stands and talks to many classmates. The teacher joins a pair only if one learner is left over.

When a learner is stuck or speaks another language to you: (1) show it: the picture, a gesture, or the board; (2) give one more short English example; (3) point to the grammar box on their page; (4) a classmate can help for a few seconds, then back to English. You don't need to understand what classmates say to each other.

Lesson 10 (Week 11): Step by Step

At a glance

Objectives: learners can…

  • give instructions in order with first, next, then, after that, finally
  • follow spoken instructions and number the steps
  • ask How do I…? What do I do next? What do I do after that?
  • give a warning with Don't… and Don't forget to…
  • read a medicine label (invented) and answer questions about it
  • write 4 steps for a task they know

Materials

  • Student Pages for Lesson 10 (print for the number expected + 3 spares)
  • Talk Time: the four step strips (on the Talk Time page)
  • phone + small speaker, L3_L10_listening.mp3
  • optional: a phone charger and a cup, to show plug in and the steps of a task
  • Prep time: 5 min.

Key vocabulary (with pictures on the New Words page)

★ instructions • ★ step • ★ press • ★ plug in • ★ turn on / turn off • ★ laundry • ★ detergent • ★ safety goggles • ★ label • ★ tablet (medicine) • ★ password • log in

Clock-time plan

Times are loose. If a step runs long, take time from Read & Write first, then from Talk Time.

TimeStepMinGrouping (15 / 7–8)If running behind
6:00–6:10Opening Talk + Homework Check10Pairs (7 pairs + 1 trio / 3–4 pairs)One card only
6:10–6:18New Words (picture page) + pair game8Whole class, then pairsTeach the ★ words only
6:18–6:30Listening: play 1 (Task A), play 2 (Tasks B and C) + "Say it"12Individuals, then pairs checkDo Task C together on the board
6:30–6:45Grammar Q&A: sequence words + imperatives; Don't…; How do I…? + pair drill15Whole class, then pairsSkip the pair drill; Talk Time practices it
6:45–7:00BREAK15
7:00–7:12Talk Time: Teach Me in Four Steps12Pairs (one learner teaches the group with 5 or fewer)2 strips only
7:12–7:17Exit Ticket + Homework5IndividualsNever skip
7:17–7:25Read & Write: a medicine label; write 4 steps8Individuals, then pairsReading questions only; the steps become homework
7:25–7:30Progress Check5IndividualsDo it in Week 12 at 6:00, while people arrive

Skip order if you're running behind: (1) the Read & Write writing task (it becomes homework); (2) the pair drill at the end of Grammar; (3) half of Talk Time (2 strips only). Never skip: the listening tasks, the grammar boxes and the mistakes table, and the exit ticket.

Attendance (15 → 7–8): every step lists both sizes. With 5 or fewer, sit at one table: one learner teaches a strip to the group, and the group mimes each step.

Step by step

Step 1 · 6:00–6:10 · Opening Talk + Homework Check · 10 min

  • Grouping: pairs, the same partner for both parts. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs.
  • Before class: write on the board: I'm good at… / I'm interested in… / I don't mind… + -ing
  • Opening Talk (6 min): learners open the Opening Talk page. A asks a card question; B answers with 2–3 sentences; A asks one follow-up. Switch after each card.
  • Model with one learner: "What are you good at?" → (answer) → "Can you give me an example?"
  • Homework Check (4 min): partners read their Lesson 9 Homework item 2 (Tell me about yourself) to each other. Walk around. Write 2 common errors on the board (often good at cook or interested on) and correct them together.
  • Late arrivals: join any pair as a group of 3.
  • If behind: one card only, then the homework check.

Step 2 · 6:10–6:18 · New Words · 8 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Show the New Words page.
  • Do: point to each picture and say the word. Learners repeat once. Mime each action: press a button, plug in a cord, turn on a light, turn it off, put on safety goggles.
  • Show step: count on your fingers: "Step 1, step 2, step 3."
  • Check meaning (1 min): "You wash clothes with…?" (detergent) • "On a medicine bottle, you read the…?" (label) • "Before you log in, you type your…?" (password)
  • Pairs (2 min): A says a word; B points to the picture and mimes it or makes a sentence (Press START.). Switch.
  • If behind: teach the ★ words only.

Step 3 · 6:18–6:30 · Listening + "Say it" · 12 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Before you listen (1 min): say: "Maria is a new worker at a supermarket. Her coworker Tom is teaching her to use a machine. What machine is it? Listen."
  • Play 1 → Task A (what machine?). Pairs compare. Check together.
  • Read Tasks B and C together (1 min) so learners know what to listen for.
  • Play 2 → Tasks B and C. Pairs compare. Then show the answers (answer key).
  • "Say it" (2 min): say: "For th in then and the, put your tongue between your teeth, and use your voice." Then third: the same tongue, no voice. Pause a little after each step. The class repeats each line in the box twice.
  • The audio plays the conversation once (about 1:11). Press play again for play 2. A third play is fine if the class needs it.
  • If behind: do Task C together on the board, reading the lines yourself.

Step 4 · 6:30–6:45 · Grammar Q&A · 15 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Show the Grammar page. The left side is the question. The right side is the answer.
  • Show it (2 min): make a cup of tea in mime and say each step: "First, boil the water. Next, put the tea bag in the cup. Then, add the water. After that, wait 3 minutes. Finally, drink it!" Hold up one finger for each step.
  • Boxes 1 and 2 (4 min): read a question from the left; the class answers from the right. Point out: no you and no -s in an instruction (Press START).
  • Box 3 (2 min): warnings: Don't + verb, Don't forget to + verb.
  • Box 4 (1 min): the five sequence words, in order. Say them; the class repeats.
  • Check questions: "___, put on your goggles. (step 1)" (First) • "___, turn it off. (the last step)" (Finally) • "Don't ___ (open) the door." (open) • "How ___ I log in?" (do)
  • Practice A and B (3 min): learners write, then pairs check. Go over the answers.
  • Pair drill (last 2 min): A asks "How do I make rice?" (or tea, a sandwich). B answers with 3 steps and sequence words. Switch.
  • If behind: skip the pair drill. Talk Time practices it.

Break · 6:45–7:00 · 15 min

  • Write on the board: First, … Next, … Then, … After that, … Finally, … and How do I…? / What do I do next? / Don't forget to…

Step 5 · 7:00–7:12 · Talk Time: Teach Me in Four Steps · 12 min

  • Grouping: pairs. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 trio. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs. 5 or fewer: one learner teaches a strip to the group, and the group mimes.
  • How it works: the Talk Time page has 4 strips. In each strip, the 4 pictures (A–D) are not in order. A chooses a strip, finds the right order (writes it under the strip), and teaches B with sequence words: First, turn on the water. Next, use soap… B mimes each step and asks What do I do next? Then switch with a new strip.
  • Model with one learner (1 min): strip 1: "First, turn on the water." (point to B) "Next, use soap." (D) … The learner mimes.
  • Rounds (8 min): about 2 minutes per strip; each pair does all 4 strips if there is time. Walk around and listen for the sequence words.
  • Finish (2 min): ask 2 pairs to teach one strip to the class.
  • If behind: 2 strips only.

Step 6 · 7:12–7:17 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP

  • Exit ticket: each learner writes two sentences on a slip: two steps for a task with sequence words (First, open the app. Then, type your password.), and one warning with Don't and a reason with because or so (Don't open the door, because the water is hot.). Collect at the door.
  • Homework: open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (one sentence on the board). Say: "About 15 minutes. Bring it next week."

Read & Write · 7:17–7:25 · A Medicine Label and 4 Steps · 8 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Say first: "This label is invented. It's for reading practice only. For real medicine, always ask a pharmacist or a doctor."
  • Read (3 min): learners read the label and answer questions 1–5. Say: "Read fast first. Then find the answers."
  • Pairs check (1 min): compare answers; check together.
  • Write (4 min): learners write 4 steps for a task they know (making coffee, washing a car, sending a text) with sequence words and one Don't.
  • If behind: questions 1–5 only; the steps become homework.

Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min

  • Grouping: individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
  • Part A: read the 4 sentences in the answer key, slowly, 2 times each. Learners circle a or b.
  • Parts B and C: learners do them alone. Walk around and help with the instructions only.
  • Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "With a little help." 😐 "Not yet."
  • Collect the pages (or check them at the start of Week 12).
  • If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 12 at 6:00, while learners arrive.

Listening script: L3_L10_listening.mp3 (about 1:11; the conversation plays once, so press play again for the second listen)

Audio: play from a phone + small speaker. No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer, at a normal, friendly speed.

Narrator: Lesson ten. Listening. Maria is a new worker at a supermarket. Her coworker Tom is teaching her to use a machine. Listen.

Tom: Hi, Maria. Welcome to the team! Today I'm going to show you the floor cleaning machine. It's easy.

Maria: Great. How do I start?

Tom: First, put on your safety goggles. Then, fill the tank with water.

Maria: Why do I need goggles?

Tom: Because the detergent can hurt your eyes. Next, add one cup of detergent. Not more!

Maria: One cup. Got it. What do I do after that?

Tom: After that, plug it in and turn it on. A green light comes on.

Maria: And then I just push it?

Tom: Right. Push it slowly. Don't leave it alone when it's on.

Maria: What do I do when I finish?

Tom: Finally, turn it off, unplug it, and empty the tank.

Maria: Thanks, Tom. Can I try it now?

Tom: Sure. Press the start button, and let's go. I'll walk with you.

Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Answer key

  • Listening Task A: c (a floor cleaning machine).
  • Listening Task B: put on safety goggles 1 • fill the tank with water 2 • add detergent 3 • plug it in and turn it on 4 • turn it off and empty the tank 5 • How much detergent? one cup • The light is green.
  • Listening Task C: 1 First, 2 Then, 3 Next, 4 After that, 5 Finally.
  • Grammar Practice A: 1 First, 2 Next, 3 Then, 4 After that, 5 Finally.
  • Grammar Practice B: 1 Press, 2 Don't open, 3 do, 4 to take, 5 Turn off.
  • Talk Time (the right order): strip 1 (washing hands) B, D, A, C • strip 2 (coffee) C, A, D, B • strip 3 (a photo) D, B, C, A • strip 4 (parking) A, D, B, C. The sentences learners say will vary.
  • Homework 1: 1 Press START. 2 Don't open the door. 3 Plug in the machine. / Plug the machine in. 4 Don't forget to take your card. Homework 2, 3, and 4: answers will vary.
  • Read & Write B: 1 1 tablet • 2 every 8 hours • 3 with food • 4 3 tablets • 5 ask a pharmacist or a doctor • Writing (C): answers will vary.
  • Progress Check Part A (the teacher says, 2 times each): 1 "First, plug it in. Then, turn it on." → a • 2 "Don't open the door." → b • 3 "After that, press START." → a • 4 "Finally, take your card." → b
  • Progress Check Part B: 1 First, 2 Press, 3 Don't, 4 Finally.
  • Progress Check Part C: answers will vary; for example 1 First, open the app. Next, type your password. Then, press LOG IN. 2 Don't forget to take your receipt.
  • Progress Check scoring: A /4 + B /4 + C /2 = /10. This is not a test grade. It shows who needs more help hearing the steps (A) and with the forms (B, C).

Teacher notes

  • The medicine label is invented (important): it is for reading practice only. Tell learners to ask a pharmacist or a doctor about real medicine. Don't give medical advice, and don't ask learners about their own medicines.
  • Instructions have no you and no -s: Press START (not You press START or Presses START). Negative: Don't + verb (Don't open).
  • Sequence words: first (step 1), next / then / after that (the middle steps, in any order), finally (the last step). A comma after each one is fine but not important.
  • Don't forget to… is a friendly reminder: Don't forget to take your card.
  • Review: You have to / You need to also give instructions: You need to plug it in first. Accept it; don't teach it again.
  • Typical mistakes this week: You press START, Presses START, No open the door, Don't forget take, Final, turn it off. Say the right form clearly; the learner repeats. Learners can read the Spanish note and the tip on their Grammar page themselves; you don't need to explain them.
  • Mixed levels: stronger learners add a Don't… warning to each strip. Newer learners use Boxes 1 and 4 as a script.

sections.title: Grammar
sections.html:
Read across. A reads from the left side. B answers from the right side. Choose one part from each column.

Grammar Box 1: How was it? (the thing: -ing)

QUESTION
How wasthe concert? / the festival?
Was the workshopinteresting?
→
ANSWER
It wasexciting! / boring.
Yes, it was. / No,it was confusing.

Grammar Box 2: How did you feel? (the person: -ed)

QUESTION
How did youfeel?
Were youinterested?
Was shetired?
→
ANSWER
I wasexcited. / bored.
Yes, I was veryinterested.
Yes, she wastired at the end.

Grammar Box 3: An opinion + a reason

QUESTION
What did youthink?
Did you likeit?
→
ANSWER
I thought it was confusing,so I left early.
Yes. I thought it was relaxing,because the music was soft.

Grammar Box 4: -ing or -ed?

THE THING: It was…THE PERSON: I was…THE THING: It was…THE PERSON: I was…
excitingexcitedrelaxingrelaxed
boringboredtiringtired
interestinginterestedsurprisingsurprised
confusingconfused

Questions and answers

Q: I'm boring or I'm bored?

A: I'm bored = I feel bored. I'm boring = people don't have fun with me!

Q: When do I use -ing?

A: For the thing or the experience: The movie was boring.

Q: When do I use -ed?

A: For the person's feeling: I was bored.

Q: How do I give an opinion?

A: I thought it was + -ing, + a reason: I thought it was exciting, because the music was great.

Practice A: Write -ing or -ed.

  1. The class was very bor____. Everyone was sleepy.
  2. I was bor____, so I went home.
  3. The museum was interest____.
  4. She was surpris____. It was her birthday party!
  5. Work was tir____ today. I worked 10 hours.
  6. The map was hard. I was confus____.

Practice B: Circle the right word.

  1. The soccer game was (exciting / excited).
  2. The kids were (exciting / excited).
  3. Are you (interesting / interested) in art?
  4. The instructions were (confusing / confused).
  5. After the beach, I felt (relaxing / relaxed).

Common mistakes

✗ Don't say✓ Say
I'm boring. (for a feeling)I'm bored.
The movie was bored.The movie was boring.
I was interesting in the museum.I was interested in the museum.
I thought was confusing.I thought it was confusing.

Nota para hispanohablantes: en español es una palabra (aburrido); en inglés son dos: I'm bored (estoy aburrido), It's boring (es aburrido). Cuidado: I'm boring quiere decir soy aburrido.

Tip for speakers of other languages: people usually feel the -ed word. Things and experiences are the -ing word.

lessons.teacher:
How to Use This Plan

You don't need to speak Spanish or any other language. Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. Each Grammar page has one short Spanish note and one tip for speakers of other languages. Learners read them on their own. You never need to read, translate, or explain them.

Instructions: use the same short task words every week: Listen. Circle. Check. Write. Work with a partner. Work in a group. Ask a follow-up question. Learners have the Task Words page from Lesson 1.

Instruction rule: Model it (do it with one learner while everyone watches), check it (ask: "Do you write or speak? How many people do you talk to?"), then go. Say less, show more.

Grouping toolkit: Pairs: turn to a neighbor; with an odd number, make one group of 3. Groups: 3–4 learners. Inside–outside circles: the inner circle faces out, the outer circle faces in; the outer circle moves one person to the right each round. Mingle: everyone stands and talks to many classmates. The teacher joins a pair only if one learner is left over.

When a learner is stuck or speaks another language to you: (1) show it: the picture, a gesture, or the board; (2) give one more short English example; (3) point to the grammar box on their page; (4) a classmate can help for a few seconds, then back to English. You don't need to understand what classmates say to each other.

Lesson 11 (Week 12): Bored or Boring?

At a glance

Objectives: learners can…

  • say how something was: It was exciting. / It was boring.
  • say how they felt: I was excited. / I was bored.
  • choose -ing (the thing, the experience) or -ed (the person's feeling)
  • give an opinion with a reason: I thought it was confusing, so I left early.
  • read three short reviews and write a 3–4 sentence review with stars

Materials

  • Student Pages for Lesson 11 (print for the number expected + 3 spares)
  • Talk Time: the six event cards (on the Talk Time page)
  • phone + small speaker, L3_L11_listening.mp3
  • optional: a sheet of paper for the class "best weekend event" board
  • Prep time: 5 min.

Key vocabulary (with pictures on the New Words page)

★ exciting / excited • ★ boring / bored • ★ interesting / interested • ★ confusing / confused • ★ relaxing / relaxed • ★ tiring / tired • ★ surprising / surprised • ★ festival • ★ concert • ★ museum • fair • review (stars)

Clock-time plan

Times are loose. If a step runs long, take time from Read & Write first, then from Talk Time.

TimeStepMinGrouping (15 / 7–8)If running behind
6:00–6:10Opening Talk + Homework Check10Pairs (7 pairs + 1 trio / 3–4 pairs)One card only
6:10–6:18New Words (picture page) + pair game8Whole class, then pairsTeach the ★ words only
6:18–6:30Listening: play 1 (Task A), play 2 (Tasks B and C) + "Say it"12Individuals, then pairs checkDo Task C together on the board
6:30–6:45Grammar Q&A: -ing / -ed; How was it? How did you feel?; I thought it was… + pair drill15Whole class, then pairsSkip the pair drill; Talk Time practices it
6:45–7:00BREAK15
7:00–7:12Talk Time: Star Ratings + the best weekend event12Pairs, then groups of 3–4Round 1 only
7:12–7:17Exit Ticket + Homework5IndividualsNever skip
7:17–7:25Read & Write: three short reviews; write a review8Individuals, then pairsReading questions only; the review becomes homework
7:25–7:30Progress Check5IndividualsDo it in Week 13 at 6:00, while people arrive

Skip order if you're running behind: (1) the Read & Write review (it becomes homework); (2) the pair drill at the end of Grammar; (3) half of Talk Time (Round 1 only). Never skip: the listening tasks, the grammar boxes and the mistakes table, and the exit ticket.

Attendance (15 → 7–8): every step lists both sizes. With 5 or fewer, do Round 1 as a circle (each person tells, the person on the left gives the stars), then Round 2 as one group.

Step by step

Step 1 · 6:00–6:10 · Opening Talk + Homework Check · 10 min

  • Grouping: pairs, the same partner for both parts. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs.
  • Before class: write on the board: First, … Next, … Then, … Finally, …
  • Opening Talk (6 min): learners open the Opening Talk page. A asks a card question; B answers with 2–3 sentences; A asks one follow-up. Switch after each card.
  • Model with one learner: "How do you make your favorite food?" → (answer) → "What do you do after that?"
  • Homework Check (4 min): partners read their Lesson 10 Homework item 2 (4 steps) to each other. The partner mimes the steps. Walk around. Write 2 common errors on the board (often You press or No open) and correct them together.
  • Late arrivals: join any pair as a group of 3.
  • If behind: one card only, then the homework check.

Step 2 · 6:10–6:18 · New Words · 8 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Show the New Words page.
  • Do: point to each picture and say both words. Learners repeat once. For each pair, point to the left picture: "It was exciting." Point to the face: "I was excited."
  • Show it with your face: yawn: "The movie was boring. I was bored." Look confused: "The map was confusing. I was confused."
  • Check meaning (1 min): "A big event in a park with food and music is a…?" (festival) • "You see old pictures and things at a…?" (museum) • "You go to hear music at a…?" (concert)
  • Pairs (2 min): A points to a picture; B says two sentences (It was relaxing. I was relaxed.). Switch.
  • If behind: teach the ★ words only.

Step 3 · 6:18–6:30 · Listening + "Say it" · 12 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Before you listen (1 min): say: "It's Monday. Elena and Luis are coworkers. They're talking about the weekend. Did they like their weekend events? Listen."
  • Play 1 → Task A (did they like it?). Pairs compare. Check together.
  • Read Tasks B and C together (1 min) so learners know what to listen for.
  • Play 2 → Tasks B and C. Pairs compare. Then show the answers (answer key).
  • "Say it" (2 min): say: "-ed has 3 sounds." Read: relaxed (t), bored (d), interested (id, one more syllable). The class repeats each word twice. Then the lines in the box.
  • The audio plays the conversation once (about 1:17). Press play again for play 2. A third play is fine if the class needs it.
  • If behind: do Task C together on the board, reading the lines yourself.

Step 4 · 6:30–6:45 · Grammar Q&A · 15 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Show the Grammar page. The left side is the question. The right side is the answer.
  • Show it (2 min): draw on the board: a TV (the thing) → a face (the person). Under the TV write boring, under the face bored. Say: "-ing is the thing. -ed is the person's feeling."
  • Boxes 1 and 2 (4 min): read a question from the left; the class answers from the right. Point out: It was… + -ing; I was… + -ed.
  • Box 3 (2 min): an opinion + a reason: I thought it was confusing, so I left early.
  • Box 4 (1 min): the -ing / -ed table; read across.
  • Check questions: "The movie was ___ (bore)." (boring) • "I was very ___ (excite)." (excited) • "Were you ___ (interest)?" (interested) • "I thought it was ___ (confuse)." (confusing)
  • Practice A and B (3 min): learners write, then pairs check. Go over the answers.
  • Pair drill (last 2 min): A asks "How was your weekend?" B answers with one -ing and one -ed word (It was relaxing. I was relaxed.). Switch.
  • If behind: skip the pair drill. Talk Time practices it.

Break · 6:45–7:00 · 15 min

  • Write on the board: How was it? It was… -ing / How did you feel? I was… -ed / I thought it was…, so…

Step 5 · 7:00–7:12 · Talk Time: Star Ratings · 12 min

  • Grouping: Round 1 pairs; Round 2 groups of 3–4. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 trio. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs, then 2 groups. 5 or fewer: one circle, then one group.
  • Round 1 (7 min): each learner chooses an event card (1–6) or a real event (a TV show or a sports game is fine). A tells B about it: how it was, how they felt, and one reason. B asks two follow-up questions and gives it 1–5 stars in the table. Switch.
  • Model with one learner (1 min): "Last Saturday, I went to the Fall Fair. It was exciting, but the lines were long, so I was tired." The learner asks: "Who did you go with? Was the food good?" → "4 stars!"
  • Round 2, groups (4 min): each group chooses "the best weekend event" for the class bulletin board and agrees on two reasons (It was exciting, and it was free.). One person reports to the class.
  • If behind: Round 1 only.

Step 6 · 7:12–7:17 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP

  • Exit ticket: each learner writes two sentences on a slip: one with -ing and one with -ed about the same event, and a reason with because or so (The concert was exciting, so I was excited all night.). Collect at the door.
  • Homework: open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (one sentence on the board). Say: "About 15 minutes. Bring it next week."

Read & Write · 7:17–7:25 · Three Short Reviews · 8 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Read (3 min): learners read the three reviews and answer questions 1–5. Say: "Read fast first. Then find the answers."
  • Pairs check (1 min): compare answers; check together.
  • Write (4 min): learners write a 3–4 sentence review of an event (or a TV show, a movie, a game) with 1–5 stars and one reason.
  • If behind: questions 1–5 only; the review becomes homework.

Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min

  • Grouping: individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
  • Part A: read the 4 sentences in the answer key, slowly, 2 times each. Learners circle a or b.
  • Parts B and C: learners do them alone. Walk around and help with the instructions only.
  • Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "With a little help." 😐 "Not yet."
  • Collect the pages (or check them at the start of Week 13).
  • If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 13 at 6:00, while learners arrive.

Listening script: L3_L11_listening.mp3 (about 1:17; the conversation plays once, so press play again for the second listen)

Audio: play from a phone + small speaker. No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer, at a normal, friendly speed.

Narrator: Lesson eleven. Listening. It's Monday morning. Elena and Luis are coworkers. They're talking about the weekend. Listen.

Luis: Hi, Elena. How was your weekend? Did you do anything fun?

Elena: It was great! I went to the food festival at Riverside Park with my sister.

Luis: Really? How was it?

Elena: It was so exciting. There was live music, and we tried food from ten countries.

Luis: Was it crowded?

Elena: Yes, very. The lines were long, so I was a little tired at the end. How about you?

Luis: I went to a photo workshop at the city museum on Sunday. I was really interested in it.

Elena: Oh, nice! Was it interesting?

Luis: Not really. I thought it was confusing. The teacher talked very fast.

Elena: Oh no. Were you bored?

Luis: Yes, I was bored, so I left early. But the museum coffee shop was really relaxing.

Elena: Next time, come to the festival with me. You'll love it!

Luis: OK. That sounds fun. Maybe next month.

Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Answer key

  • Listening Task A: Elena (the food festival) 😀 • Luis (the photo workshop) 😐.
  • Listening Task B: 1 c (exciting) • 2 a (tired) • 3 e (confusing) • 4 d (bored) • 5 b (relaxing).
  • Listening Task C: 1 exciting, 2 tired, 3 interesting, 4 confusing, 5 bored, 6 relaxing.
  • Grammar Practice A: 1 boring, 2 bored, 3 interesting, 4 surprised, 5 tiring, 6 confused.
  • Grammar Practice B: 1 exciting, 2 excited, 3 interested, 4 confusing, 5 relaxed.
  • Talk Time: answers will vary.
  • Homework 1: 1 The movie was boring. 2 I was tired after work. 3 The museum was interesting. 4 She was surprised. Homework 2, 3, and 4: answers will vary.
  • Read & Write B: 1 the Fall Fair (5 stars) • 2 Music in the Park (2 stars) • 3 it was confusing; the teacher talked fast, but the library helper was patient • 4 the music started late, and it was too loud, so they were tired and left early • 5 the food (the apple pie) and the rides for kids • Writing (C): answers will vary.
  • Progress Check Part A (the teacher says, 2 times each): 1 "The concert was boring." → a • 2 "I was surprised." → b • 3 "The museum was interesting." → a • 4 "We were tired, so we left." → b
  • Progress Check Part B: 1 exciting, 2 bored, 3 confusing, 4 relaxed.
  • Progress Check Part C: answers will vary; for example 1 The festival was exciting. I was excited. 2 I thought it was boring, so I left early.
  • Progress Check scoring: A /4 + B /4 + C /2 = /10. This is not a test grade. It shows who needs more help hearing the endings (A) and choosing -ing / -ed (B, C).

Teacher notes

  • General events only (important): use community events, TV, movies, or sports. Learners never have to share where they spend their money or free time; the event cards are always an option.
  • The one rule: -ing = the thing or the experience (The movie was boring). -ed = how the person feels (I was bored).
  • Careful: I'm boring means people don't enjoy talking to me. Learners laugh when they hear it; use that.
  • I thought it was… gives an opinion in the past: I thought it was confusing, so I left early. Accept I think it was… too.
  • -ed sounds: /t/ after x, k, s, sh, ch, p (relaxed); /id/ after t, d (interested, one more syllable); /d/ for the rest (bored, tired, surprised). Don't teach the rule; just model and repeat.
  • Typical mistakes this week: I'm boring (for bored), It was excited, I was interesting in the museum, The movie was bored, I thought was confusing. Say the right form clearly; the learner repeats. Learners can read the Spanish note and the tip on their Grammar page themselves; you don't need to explain them.
  • Mixed levels: stronger learners add a second reason and a recommendation (You should go!). Newer learners use Boxes 1 and 2 as a script.

Questions and answers

Q: I didn't see nothing?

A: No. One negative only: I didn't see anything. or I saw nothing.

Q: something or anything?

A: something in + sentences: Something is wrong. anything in questions and with not: Is anything wrong?

Q: no one or nobody?

A: The same meaning: No one is home. / Nobody is home.

Q: How do I start a repair call?

A: Hi, this is… in apartment… Something is wrong with my…

✗ Don't say✓ Say

How to Use This Plan

You don't need to speak Spanish or any other language. Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. Each Grammar page has one short Spanish note and one tip for speakers of other languages. Learners read them on their own. You never need to read, translate, or explain them.

Instructions: use the same short task words every week: Listen. Circle. Check. Write. Work with a partner. Work in a group. Ask a follow-up question. Learners have the Task Words page from Lesson 1.

Instruction rule: Model it (do it with one learner while everyone watches), check it (ask: "Do you write or speak? How many people do you talk to?"), then go. Say less, show more.

Grouping toolkit: Pairs: turn to a neighbor; with an odd number, make one group of 3. Groups: 3–4 learners. Inside–outside circles: the inner circle faces out, the outer circle faces in; the outer circle moves one person to the right each round. Mingle: everyone stands and talks to many classmates. The teacher joins a pair only if one learner is left over.

When a learner is stuck or speaks another language to you: (1) show it: the picture, a gesture, or the board; (2) give one more short English example; (3) point to the grammar box on their page; (4) a classmate can help for a few seconds, then back to English. You don't need to understand what classmates say to each other.

Lesson 12 (Week 13): Something's Wrong

At a glance

Objectives: learners can…

  • say what's wrong in a home: Something is wrong with the heater. The sink is leaking.
  • use something / anything / nothing and someone / anyone / no one
  • ask for a repair and agree on a day and time: Can you send someone? Is anyone home on Tuesday?
  • use one negative only: I didn't see anything. (not I didn't see nothing)
  • read a maintenance request and write a short one (3–5 sentences)

Materials

  • Student Pages for Lesson 12 (print for the number expected + 3 spares)
  • Talk Time: the Tenant Cards, the Repair Schedule, and the apartment picture (on the Talk Time pages)
  • phone + small speaker, L3_L12_listening.mp3
  • Prep time: 5 min (Round 1 is back to back: put chairs in pairs, back to back, if you can).

Key vocabulary (with pictures on the New Words page)

★ landlord • ★ repair person • ★ maintenance request • ★ leak • ★ sink • ★ toilet • ★ heater • ★ light bulb • ★ lock • ★ smoke alarm • mouse • cockroach

Clock-time plan

Times are loose. If a step runs long, take time from Read & Write first, then from Talk Time.

TimeStepMinGrouping (15 / 7–8)If running behind

6:10–6:18New Words (picture page) + pair game8Whole class, then pairsTeach the ★ words only
6:18–6:30Listening: play 1 (Task A), play 2 (Tasks B and C) + "Say it"12Individuals, then pairs checkDo Task C together on the board
6:30–6:45Grammar Q&A: something / anything / nothing; someone / anyone / no one + pair drill15Whole class, then pairsSkip the pair drill; Talk Time practices it
6:45–7:00BREAK15
7:00–7:12Talk Time: The Repair Call + Find Something12Pairs, back to backRound 1 only

7:17–7:25Read & Write: a maintenance request; write one8Individuals, then pairsReading questions only; the request becomes homework

Skip order if you're running behind: (1) the Read & Write request (it becomes homework); (2) the pair drill at the end of Grammar; (3) half of Talk Time (Round 1 only). Never skip: the listening tasks, the grammar boxes and the mistakes table, and the exit ticket.

Attendance (15 → 7–8): every step lists both sizes. With 5 or fewer, one learner is the building manager with the schedule, and the others call one by one; then change managers.

Step by step

Step 1 · 6:00–6:10 · Opening Talk + Homework Check · 10 min

  • Grouping: pairs, the same partner for both parts. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs.
  • Before class: write on the board: How was it? It was… -ing / I was… -ed
  • Opening Talk (6 min): learners open the Opening Talk page. A asks a card question; B answers with 2–3 sentences; A asks one follow-up. Switch after each card.
  • Model with one learner: "What was the last movie you saw? How was it?" → (answer) → "How did you feel at the end?"
  • Homework Check (4 min): partners read their Lesson 11 Homework item 2 to each other. Walk around. Write 2 common errors on the board (often I was boring or It was excited) and correct them together.
  • Late arrivals: join any pair as a group of 3.
  • If behind: one card only, then the homework check.

Step 2 · 6:10–6:18 · New Words · 8 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Show the New Words page.
  • Do: point to each picture and say the word. Learners repeat once. Mime: water drops from a leak, try a door with a broken lock, cover your ears for a smoke alarm: "Beep! Beep!"
  • Show landlord and repair person: "The landlord owns the building. The repair person fixes things."
  • Check meaning (1 min): "Water is coming from the pipe. It's a…?" (leak) • "The room is cold. What's wrong?" (the heater) • "You write about a problem on a…?" (maintenance request)
  • Pairs (2 min): A says a word; B points to the picture and makes a sentence (The sink is leaking.). Switch.
  • If behind: teach the ★ words only.

Step 3 · 6:18–6:30 · Listening + "Say it" · 12 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Before you listen (1 min): say: "Sara lives in an apartment. She's calling the building office. What problems does she have? Listen."
  • Play 1 → Task A (which problems?). Pairs compare. Check together.
  • Read Tasks B and C together (1 min) so learners know what to listen for.
  • Play 2 → Tasks B and C. Pairs compare. Then show the answers (answer key).
  • "Say it" (2 min): say: "Stress the first part: SOMEthing, ANyone, NO one." Then thing: tongue between the teeth, th (not ting). The class repeats each word twice, then the line in the box.
  • The audio plays the conversation once (about 1:16). Press play again for play 2. A third play is fine if the class needs it.
  • If behind: do Task C together on the board, reading the lines yourself.

Step 4 · 6:30–6:45 · Grammar Q&A · 15 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Show the Grammar page. The left side is the question. The right side is the answer.
  • Show it (2 min): look into an empty cup: "Is there anything in it? No, there isn't anything. There's nothing in it." Look at the door: "Is anyone at the door? No, no one is there."
  • Boxes 1, 2, and 3 (5 min): read a question from the left; the class answers from the right.
  • Box 4 (2 min): the table: some- in + sentences, any- in questions and with not, no- alone. Point to the one-negative rule: I didn't see anything = I saw nothing.
  • Check questions: "Is ___ wrong?" (anything) • "Yes, ___ is wrong with the sink." (something) • "No, ___ is home." (no one) • "I didn't hear ___." (anything)
  • Practice A and B (3 min): learners write, then pairs check. Go over the answers.
  • Pair drill (last 2 min): A points to a picture on the New Words page: "Is anything wrong with the ___?" B answers: Yes, something is wrong with it. It's… or No, nothing is wrong. Switch.
  • If behind: skip the pair drill. Talk Time practices it.

Break · 6:45–7:00 · 15 min

  • Write on the board: Is anything wrong? / Something is wrong with… / Is anyone home? / No one is home. / Can you send someone? Turn pairs of chairs back to back for Round 1.

Step 5 · 7:00–7:12 · Talk Time: The Repair Call · 12 min

  • Grouping: pairs, back to back (like a phone call: no looking!). 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 trio (two tenants). 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs. 5 or fewer: one manager, the others call one by one.
  • Round 1 (7 min): A is a tenant with a Tenant Card; B is the building manager with the Repair Schedule. A calls: says what's wrong and since when. B asks one question (Is there any water on the floor?) and finds an open time when someone is home. They agree on a day and time; B writes it in the schedule. Switch roles with a new card.
  • Model with one learner (1 min): you are the tenant with card 1: "Hi, this is apartment 3A. Something is wrong with my toilet. It's leaking." The manager: "Is anyone home on Monday at 4:00?" → "Yes, someone is home after 3."
  • Round 2, Find Something (4 min): pairs look at the apartment picture and find 7 problems. They say There's something wrong with the… / There's a… on the… / There isn't anything wrong with the chair. The first pair to find all 7 wins.
  • If behind: Round 1 only.

Step 6 · 7:12–7:17 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP

  • Exit ticket: each learner writes two sentences on a slip: one with something / anything / nothing or someone / anyone / no one (Something is wrong with my heater.), and one with if or so (No one is home in the morning, so please come at 3.). Collect at the door.
  • Homework: open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (one sentence on the board). Say: "About 15 minutes. Bring it next week."

Read & Write · 7:17–7:25 · A Maintenance Request · 8 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Read (3 min): learners read the request form and Ken's note and answer questions 1–5. Say: "Read fast first. Then find the answers."
  • Pairs check (1 min): compare answers; check together.
  • Write (4 min): learners write a 3–5 sentence maintenance request: the problem, since when, the best time, and a phone number. Say: "Invent the apartment, the problem, and a 555 number."
  • If behind: questions 1–5 only; the request becomes homework.

Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min

  • Grouping: individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
  • Part A: read the 4 sentences in the answer key, slowly, 2 times each. Learners circle a or b.
  • Parts B and C: learners do them alone. Walk around and help with the instructions only.
  • Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "With a little help." 😐 "Not yet."
  • Collect the pages (or check them at the start of Week 14).
  • If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 14 at 6:00, while learners arrive.

Listening script: L3_L12_listening.mp3 (about 1:16; the conversation plays once, so press play again for the second listen)

Audio: play from a phone + small speaker. No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer, at a normal, friendly speed.

Narrator: Lesson twelve. Listening. Sara lives in an apartment. She's calling the building office about some problems. Listen.

Mr. Grant: Maple Court Apartments, this is Mr. Grant. How can I help you?

Sara: Hi, this is Sara in apartment 4B. Something is wrong with my kitchen sink. It's leaking.

Mr. Grant: Oh no. Is there any water on the floor?

Sara: Yes, a little. I put a towel under it. And there's something else. The heater doesn't work.

Mr. Grant: Do you see anything on the screen?

Sara: No, I don't see anything. The screen is black, and the apartment is really cold.

Mr. Grant: OK. I'll send someone tomorrow morning. Is anyone home at nine?

Sara: No, no one is home in the morning. I work until two.

Mr. Grant: How about Tuesday at three?

Sara: Tuesday at three is fine. If it gets worse tonight, I'll call you.

Mr. Grant: Great. The repair person will fix both things. Until then, don't use the sink.

Sara: OK, I won't. Thank you so much.

Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Answer key

  • Listening Task A: ✓ the kitchen sink (it's leaking) and ✓ the heater (it doesn't work). ✗ the toilet, ✗ the lock, ✗ a mouse.
  • Listening Task B: 1 4B • 2 a little water • 3 black • 4 Tuesday • 5 3:00.
  • Listening Task C: 1 Something, 2 any, 3 something, 4 anything, 5 someone, 6 anyone, 7 no one.
  • Grammar Practice A: 1 something, 2 anything, 3 nothing, 4 someone, 5 anyone, 6 No one.
  • Grammar Practice B: 1 anything, 2 someone, 3 anything, 4 nothing, 5 anyone.
  • Talk Time Round 1 (possible open times): card 1 → Mon 4:00 or Tue 4:00 • card 2 → Tue 9:00 or Fri 1:00 • card 3 → Thu 9:00 or Thu 1:00 • card 4 → Mon 1:00, Mon 4:00, or Fri 1:00. The conversations will vary.
  • Talk Time Round 2 (7 problems): the smoke alarm is beeping • the light bulb is out (off) • the sink is leaking • the heater doesn't work (it's cold) • the door lock is open / broken • a cockroach on the wall • a mouse on the floor. (Nothing is wrong with the plant, the chair, or the picture.)
  • Homework 1: 1 Something is wrong with the heater. 2 Is anyone home? 3 I didn't see anything. / I saw nothing. 4 No one called. Homework 2, 3, and 4: answers will vary.
  • Read & Write B: 1 apartment 2C • 2 the bathroom light (it doesn't turn on) and the lock on the front door (it's hard to close) • 3 since last Friday • 4 after 5:00 p.m. on weekdays, or Saturday • 5 call or text Ken at 555-0191 • Writing (C): answers will vary.
  • Progress Check Part A (the teacher says, 2 times each): 1 "Something is wrong with the sink." → a • 2 "No one is home on Monday." → b • 3 "I didn't see anything." → b • 4 "I'll send someone on Friday." → a
  • Progress Check Part B: 1 anything, 2 Someone, 3 anything, 4 no one.
  • Progress Check Part C: answers will vary; for example 1 Something is wrong with my heater. It doesn't work. 2 Can you send someone on Tuesday after 3:00?
  • Progress Check scoring: A /4 + B /4 + C /2 = /10. This is not a test grade. It shows who needs more help hearing some- / any- / no- (A) and with the forms (B, C).

Teacher notes

  • Keep it practical and invented (important): never ask about learners' real rent, landlord, or living situation. Use the cards and invented apartments. Tenant rights are a Level 5 topic; if a learner asks, point to the local resources on the "Keep practicing" sheet.
  • The rule in one line: some- in + sentences (Something is wrong), any- in questions and with not (Is anything wrong? I didn't see anything), no- alone (Nothing is wrong. No one is home).
  • One negative only: I didn't see anything or I saw nothing (not I didn't see nothing).
  • Something is wrong with… is the most useful sentence today. Practice it with many nouns.
  • Review: If it gets worse, I'll call you (Lesson 6) and I'll send someone (Lesson 5). Accept both; don't teach them again.
  • Typical mistakes this week: I didn't see nothing, Is something wrong? (OK in real life, but teach anything first), Nobody is not home, Anything is wrong (in a + sentence), some one as two words. Say the right form clearly; the learner repeats. Learners can read the Spanish note and the tip on their Grammar page themselves; you don't need to explain them.
  • Mixed levels: stronger learners add since… and an If…, I'll… sentence to each call. Newer learners use Boxes 1 and 2 as a script.

sections.title: Grammar
sections.html:
Read across. A reads from the left side. B answers from the right side. Choose one part from each column.

Grammar Box 1: going to (a plan)

QUESTION
What are yougoing to do next year?
Are yougoing to apply?
When are youmeeting the counselor?
→
ANSWER
I'm going totake a computer class.
Yes, I'm going toapply in January.
I'm meetingthe counselor on Monday.

Grammar Box 2: hope to / I hope I'll (a hope)

QUESTION
What do youhope to do?
What do youplan to / want to do?
→
ANSWER
I hope toget my diploma.
I hope I'llhave my own business.
I plan to / I want tosave money for a car.

Grammar Box 3: will (decided now, a promise)

QUESTION
What will youdo first?
Can youcall them?
→
ANSWER
First, I'llask about classes at the community college.
OK, I'llcall them tomorrow.

Grammar Box 4: Which one?

MEANINGEXAMPLE
going toalready plannedI'm going to take a class in January.
will ('ll)decided now, or a promiseOK, I'll call the college tomorrow.
hope to / I hope I'llI want it, but I'm not sureI hope to get a promotion.
plan to / want tomy idea for the futureI plan to save money.

Questions and answers

Q: I hope get or I hope to get?

A: I hope to get. hope to + verb.

Q: I hope I will to have?

A: No. I hope I'll have my own business. (no to after will)

Q: I'm going to study or I'm going to studying?

A: I'm going to study. going to + verb (no -ing).

Q: What is gonna?

A: Fast speech for going to. Understand it; in your talk, say going to.

Practice A: Write going to, 'll, or hope to.

  1. I bought the books. I'm ____________ start the class on Monday. (planned)
  2. The phone is ringing. I____________ get it! (decided now)
  3. I ____________ get a promotion, but I'm not sure. (a hope)
  4. She's ____________ take the driving test in May. (planned)
  5. Don't worry. I____________ help you with your talk. (a promise)

Practice B: Circle the right words.

  1. I hope (to get / get) my diploma.
  2. (I'll / I'll to) call the college tomorrow.
  3. We're (going to / going) open a small business.
  4. I plan (save / to save) money for a car.
  5. I hope (I'll / I will to) have a better job.

Common mistakes

✗ Don't say✓ Say
I hope get my diploma.I hope to get my diploma.
I will to study English.I will study English.
I'm going to studying.I'm going to study.
I plan save money.I plan to save money.

Nota para hispanohablantes: I hope to… = Espero… + infinitivo (Espero conseguir…). I hope I'll… = Espero que…. En inglés no se necesita una forma especial del verbo después de I hope.

Tip for speakers of other languages: going to = already planned. will = decided now or a promise. hope to = you want it, but you're not sure.

lessons.teacher:
How to Use This Plan

You don't need to speak Spanish or any other language. Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. Each Grammar page has one short Spanish note and one tip for speakers of other languages. Learners read them on their own. You never need to read, translate, or explain them.

Instructions: use the same short task words every week: Listen. Circle. Check. Write. Work with a partner. Work in a group. Ask a follow-up question. Learners have the Task Words page from Lesson 1.

Instruction rule: Model it (do it with one learner while everyone watches), check it (ask: "Do you write or speak? How many people do you talk to?"), then go. Say less, show more.

Grouping toolkit: Pairs: turn to a neighbor; with an odd number, make one group of 3. Groups: 3–4 learners. Inside–outside circles: the inner circle faces out, the outer circle faces in; the outer circle moves one person to the right each round. Mingle: everyone stands and talks to many classmates. The teacher joins a pair only if one learner is left over.

When a learner is stuck or speaks another language to you: (1) show it: the picture, a gesture, or the board; (2) give one more short English example; (3) point to the grammar box on their page; (4) a classmate can help for a few seconds, then back to English. You don't need to understand what classmates say to each other.

Lesson 13 (Week 14): Where I'm Going

At a glance

Objectives: learners can…

  • talk about a plan with going to: I'm going to take a computer class.
  • talk about hopes with hope to / I hope I'll: I hope to get my diploma.
  • say what they will do first to reach a goal: First, I'll ask about classes.
  • choose going to (planned), will (decided now, a promise), or hope to (not sure)
  • read a community college flyer and write a graduation talk (6–8 sentences)
  • give a 1–2 minute talk about their goals: Then → Now → Next

Materials

  • Student Pages for Lesson 13 (print for the number expected + 3 spares)
  • Talk Time: the Goal Ladder and the Feedback Cards (on the Talk Time pages)
  • phone + small speaker, L3_L13_listening.mp3
  • Your own 1-minute talk (prepare it before class; see Step 5)
  • Prep time: 10 min.

Key vocabulary (with pictures on the New Words page)

★ plan • ★ hope • ★ decide • ★ diploma • ★ certificate • ★ career • ★ promotion • ★ save money • ★ own business • ★ driver's license • ★ computer class • community college

Clock-time plan

Times are loose. If a step runs long, take time from Read & Write first, then from Talk Time.

Skip order if you're running behind: (1) the Read & Write talk (it becomes homework); (2) the pair drill at the end of Grammar; (3) half of Talk Time (the ladder only). Never skip: the listening tasks, the grammar boxes and the mistakes table, and the exit ticket.

Attendance (15 → 7–8): every step lists both sizes. With 5 or fewer, everyone rehearses the talk for the whole group; each listener says one thing they liked.

Step by step

Step 1 · 6:00–6:10 · Opening Talk + Homework Check · 10 min

  • Grouping: pairs, the same partner for both parts. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs.
  • Before class: write on the board: Is anything wrong? Something is wrong with… / No one is home.
  • Opening Talk (6 min): learners open the Opening Talk page. A asks a card question; B answers with 2–3 sentences; A asks one follow-up. Switch after each card.
  • Model with one learner: "What did you do this year that you're proud of?" → (answer) → "How did you do it?"
  • Homework Check (4 min): partners read their Lesson 12 Homework item 2 to each other. Walk around. Write 2 common errors on the board (often I didn't see nothing or Anything is wrong) and correct them together.
  • Late arrivals: join any pair as a group of 3.
  • If behind: one card only, then the homework check.

Step 2 · 6:10–6:18 · New Words · 8 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Show the New Words page.
  • Do: point to each picture and say the word. Learners repeat once.
  • Show diploma and certificate: "A diploma is from a school, like high school. A certificate is for a job skill, like a medical assistant or a forklift driver."
  • Check meaning (1 min): "You get a better job at the same company. It's a…?" (promotion) • "You put money in the bank every month. You…?" (save money) • "You need it to drive a car." (a driver's license)
  • Pairs (2 min): A says a word; B points to the picture and makes a sentence about a goal (I hope to get my driver's license.). Switch.
  • If behind: teach the ★ words only.

Step 3 · 6:18–6:30 · Listening + "Say it" · 12 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Before you listen (1 min): say: "Sofia was a Level 3 student. Tonight she's visiting the class. She's talking about her goals. What is her main goal? Listen."
  • Play 1 → Task A (her main goal). Pairs compare. Check together.
  • Read Tasks B and C together (1 min) so learners know what to listen for.
  • Play 2 → Tasks B and C. Pairs compare. Then show the answers (answer key).
  • "Say it" (2 min): say: "In a talk, pause after each idea, and stress the important word." Read the line in the box with pauses. Then: "People often say going to as gonna. You can understand it; you don't need to say it." The class repeats the line twice.
  • The audio plays the talk once (about 1:09). Press play again for play 2. A third play is fine if the class needs it.
  • If behind: do Task C together on the board, reading the lines yourself.

Step 4 · 6:30–6:45 · Grammar Q&A · 15 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Show the Grammar page. The left side is the question. The right side is the answer.
  • Show it (2 min): write three sentences on the board: I'm going to take a class in January. (planned) • OK, I'll call the college tomorrow. (decided now) • I hope to get a better job. (I want it, but I'm not sure).
  • Boxes 1, 2, and 3 (5 min): read a question from the left; the class answers from the right. Point out: hope to + verb, but I hope I'll + verb.
  • Box 4 (2 min): which one? Read the table. Then plan to / want to / hope to + verb.
  • Check questions: "I ___ get my diploma." (hope to) • "Next year, I'm ___ take a computer class." (going to) • "The phone is ringing. I ___ get it!" ('ll) • "I hope I ___ have my own business." ('ll)
  • Practice A and B (3 min): learners write, then pairs check. Go over the answers.
  • Pair drill (last 2 min): A asks "What are you going to do next year?" B answers and adds one I hope to… (I'm going to save money. I hope to buy a car.). Switch.
  • If behind: skip the pair drill. Talk Time practices it.

Break · 6:45–7:00 · 15 min

  • Write on the board: Then: … years ago, I… / Now: I… / Next: I'm going to… I hope to… and First, I'll…

Step 5 · 7:00–7:12 · Talk Time: Goal Ladder + Talk Rehearsal · 12 min

  • Grouping: pairs, then groups of 3. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 trio, then 5 groups of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs, then 2–3 groups. 5 or fewer: one group.
  • Model your own talk first (1 min): give your 1-minute talk (Then → Now → Next, one reason). Example: "Ten years ago, I was a cook. Now I'm a volunteer teacher. Next year, I'm going to take a Spanish class, because I want to understand my neighbors. I hope to visit Mexico." Point to each part on the board as you speak.
  • Goal Ladder, pairs (4 min): each learner fills in the ladder on the Talk Time page for one goal (step 1: I'll…; step 2: I'm going to…; top: I hope to…). Then explains it to a partner, who asks two follow-up questions.
  • Talk Rehearsal, groups of 3 (6 min): each learner gives the talk (Then → Now → Next, with a reason), reading from the frame is fine. The 2 listeners fill in a Feedback Card: one thing I liked and one tip. About 2 minutes per speaker.
  • If behind: the ladder only; the rehearsal becomes homework (practice at home with a family member).

Step 6 · 7:12–7:17 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP

  • Exit ticket: each learner writes two sentences on a slip: one with going to or hope to (I hope to get my driver's license.), and one with I'll and because or so (First, I'll study the book, because the test is hard.). Collect at the door.
  • Homework: open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (one sentence on the board). Say: "About 15 minutes. Next week is the final exam. In Week 16, you'll give your talk at graduation."

Read & Write · 7:17–7:25 · A College Flyer and the Graduation Talk · 8 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Read (3 min): learners read the flyer and answer questions 1–5. Say: "Read fast first. Then find the answers."
  • Pairs check (1 min): compare answers; check together.
  • Write (4 min): learners start their graduation talk (6–8 sentences) with the talk frame. They finish it at home.
  • If behind: questions 1–5 only; the talk becomes homework.

Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min

  • Grouping: individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
  • Part A: read the 4 sentences in the answer key, slowly, 2 times each. Learners circle a or b.
  • Parts B and C: learners do them alone. Walk around and help with the instructions only.
  • Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "With a little help." 😐 "Not yet."
  • Collect the pages (or check them in Week 15 before the final).
  • If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 15 at 6:00, before the final exam.

Listening script: L3_L13_listening.mp3 (about 1:09; the talk plays once, so press play again for the second listen)

Audio: play from a phone + small speaker. No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer, at a normal, friendly speed.

Narrator: Lesson thirteen. Listening. Sofia was a Level 3 student. Tonight, she's talking to the class about her goals. Listen.

Mr. Novak: Welcome back, Sofia! Please tell us about your goals.

Sofia: Thank you. Three years ago, I came to this class. I was nervous, and my English was not very good.

Sofia: Now I work at a hotel, and I can talk with my coworkers in English.

Mr. Novak: That's great. What's your main goal?

Sofia: My main goal is to get a medical assistant certificate. I hope to work at a clinic.

Mr. Novak: How are you going to do that?

Sofia: First, I'm going to take a computer class at the community college. It starts in January.

Sofia: After that, I'll apply for the certificate program. And I hope to help my kids with their homework, too.

Mr. Novak: Any advice for the class?

Sofia: Yes. Come every week, and don't be afraid to make mistakes. You can do it!

Mr. Novak: Thank you, Sofia. Good luck!

Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Answer key

  • Listening Task A: b (a medical assistant certificate).
  • Listening Task B: came to this class 1 • works at a hotel 2 • take a computer class 3 • apply for the certificate program 4 • work at a clinic 5 • When does the class start? January • Where does she work now? a hotel.
  • Listening Task C: 1 hope to, 2 going to, 3 going to, 4 'll (I'll), 5 hope to.
  • Grammar Practice A: 1 going to, 2 'll, 3 hope to, 4 going to, 5 'll.
  • Grammar Practice B: 1 to get, 2 I'll, 3 going to, 4 to save, 5 I'll.
  • Talk Time: answers will vary.
  • Homework 1: 1 I'm going to take a computer class. 2 I hope to get my diploma. 3 I hope I'll have my own business. 4 I'll call the college tomorrow. Homework 2, 3, and 4: answers will vary.
  • Read & Write B: 1 free • 2 Computer Basics (Monday and Wednesday, 6:00–8:00 p.m.) • 3 on Saturdays, 9:00 a.m.–12:00 p.m. • 4 at the Welcome Center, Room 101 • 5 Friday, January 15, at 6:30 p.m. • Writing (C): answers will vary.
  • Progress Check Part A (the teacher says, 2 times each): 1 "I'm going to take a class in March." → a • 2 "I hope to open my own business." → b • 3 "OK, I'll call them tomorrow." → b • 4 "I'm meeting the counselor on Monday." → a
  • Progress Check Part B: 1 to get, 2 going to, 3 I'll, 4 to.
  • Progress Check Part C: answers will vary; for example 1 I'm going to save money for a car. 2 I hope to get a promotion.
  • Progress Check scoring: A /4 + B /4 + C /2 = /10. This is not a test grade. It shows who needs more help hearing the future forms (A) and with the forms (B, C).

Teacher notes

  • Goals are personal (important): every goal is a good goal. "Learn more English" and "help my kids" are great goals. Learners don't have to share personal details; an invented goal is fine. Don't ask about immigration status, money, or family problems.
  • Model your talk first: your own 1-minute talk shows the shape (Then → Now → Next) better than any explanation. Keep it simple.
  • Three forms, three meanings: going to = already planned (I'm going to take a class in January). will = decided now or a promise (OK, I'll call them). hope to = you want it, but you're not sure (I hope to work at a clinic).
  • hope to + verb; I hope I'll + verb. Both are fine. I hope I will to… is wrong.
  • gonna: learners will hear it everywhere. They only need to understand it; in their talk, they say going to.
  • Graduation (Week 16): learners may read their talk from paper. Next week (Week 15) is the final exam; remind learners to bring their talk draft to graduation.
  • Typical mistakes this week: I hope get, I will to study, I'm going to studying, I hope I will to…, I plan study. Say the right form clearly; the learner repeats. Learners can read the Spanish note and the tip on their Grammar page themselves; you don't need to explain them.
  • Mixed levels: stronger learners add a reason to every step and a time (in January, next year). Newer learners use the talk frame word for word.
